ai-avatars-headshots-6.territory: The seller is between packing orders, worried the shop looks stitched together from fifty different photo sessions. The tone hint says visual playground, but for this product the play is in the merchandise, not the chrome: the interface answers with the calm of a rented photo studio, neutral walls, one saved lighting rig, everything repeatable. The feeling delivered is factory confidence: press the button, get the same result, every time.

palette.note: The UI stays studio-gray and color-mute so product photos read true to color; the single teal accent marks only template actions and never competes with merchandise.

ai-avatars-headshots-6.typography: Söhne for everything, set small and even like equipment labels; the products are the display type, the interface speaks in captions.
ai-avatars-headshots-6.motif: The matte frame: every photo in the app sits inside the seller's saved template rendered as a thin physical passe-partout, so on-template and off-template listings are visibly different objects at a glance.

ia.coreObject: The store template (backdrop, lighting, shadow, padding, export sizes) applied across a product catalog
ia.primaryLoop: New products come in from the workbench, get dropped through the saved template, and land in the catalog grid already matching the other forty-nine; the seller returns every time they list something new.

ai-chatbot-2.territory: Hands on the wheel at 70 mph, or eyes that stopped cooperating years ago: the user cannot look, only ask. The interface answers as a capable counterpart sitting shotgun: one enormous button findable by feel, short answers spoken first, and every visual element merely a mirror of what the voice already did. Nothing on screen is required.

palette.note: Every pairing clears WCAG AAA at 200% text size on true OLED black; yellow marks exactly one thing, the talk button, so it can be found at arm's length or in peripheral vision.

ai-chatbot-2.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible, the typeface designed by the Braille Institute, with the transcript set at 24 pt minimum and every size following system accessibility settings without breaking layout.
ai-chatbot-2.motif: The ripple: concentric rings breathing out from the hold-to-talk button while you speak and while it answers, readable as motion from the corner of an eye and mirrored as haptic pulses for no eyes at all.

ia.coreObject: The exchange: a spoken question and a short spoken answer
ia.primaryLoop: Hold, ask, hear two sentences, back to the road; the text history waits for after the trip.

ai-image-generation-2.territory: The author is deep in production — chapter twelve, panel forty — and their one fear is drift: the hero coming back from the generator wearing a stranger's face. The interface answers like a working backstage: a dark, matte stage where the images are the only light, and the character stands in the wings of every screen, locked and unmistakably themselves.

palette.note: Matte charcoal with zero gradients so generated frames read like lit prints in a darkroom; tungsten amber marks the locked state and only the locked state.

ai-image-generation-2.typography: General Sans for UI (dry, technical, no flourish), JetBrains Mono for scene numbers, seeds and export filenames — the type behaves like a production slate, not a hype poster.
ai-image-generation-2.motif: The turnaround strip — every character exists as a fixed three-view strip (front, three-quarter, profile) that docks at the bottom of any scene screen, physically present as the proof of the lock.

ia.coreObject: the locked character inside a project
ia.primaryLoop: Write one line of scene direction, generate, keep or reroll; the strip at the bottom guarantees who shows up, so the series grows a few panels every night.

ai-writing-4.territory: The author opens a draft afraid of two things at once: shipping a clumsy sentence, and shipping a sentence that isn't theirs. The focused writing studio from the tone hint becomes a private study: manuscript in the middle, everything else in the margins. The interface answers with the manner of a trusted human copyeditor, it suggests in pencil, cites the author's own past work as the authority, and never overwrites a word without consent.

palette.note: Warm paper and ink everywhere; the red-pencil accent exists only in the margins and score chips, the manuscript body is never colored by the tool.

ai-writing-4.typography: Tiempos Text carries the manuscript at reading size, Söhne handles chrome two sizes smaller; the draft is always the largest thing on screen, which is the whole personality.
ai-writing-4.motif: Margin pencil marks: every edit lives beside the text as a hand-set annotation citing the author's own corpus ('you cut this phrase in 19 of 23 pieces'), never as an inline rewrite.

ia.coreObject: A draft with a voice profile attached
ia.primaryLoop: Paste today's draft, walk the margin marks accepting or declining, watch the voice-match score settle, ship; the author returns with every new piece.

astrology-3.territory: Morning coffee, cards on the table, the small thrill of turning one over before the day starts. The mystic night sky from the tone hint stays, but this is a study practice, not a fortune booth: wonder with a spine of discipline. The interface answers with candlelit quiet and the patience of a good teacher, it never reads for you, it waits while you remember.

palette.note: Deep indigo night with candle-cream text; gold is reserved for card frames and mastered cards, so progress literally gilds the deck over months.

astrology-3.typography: Canela for card names and headlines with old engraving warmth, Untitled Sans for meanings and UI; the serif appears only where the cards speak.
astrology-3.motif: The gilt frame: the fine gold line-border of a Rider-Waite card is the app's one container, and it closes fully only around cards you've truly learned, leaving unlearned cards with an unfinished corner.

ia.coreObject: A card in your memory (one of 78, each with upright and reversed meanings and your journal history)
ia.primaryLoop: Draw the morning card, answer one recall question, write a line in the journal; spaced repetition decides tomorrow's review, and the daily ritual brings you back.

baby-tracking-7.territory: It is 3:12 AM, the baby is finally down, and the parent's eyes hurt. The tone hint's tenderness and reassurance become the whole brief: an interface that whispers, never glows, and answers the only question that matters, when is the next window. The feeling delivered is a calm night nurse who knows this specific baby and explains herself in one plain sentence.

palette.note: Warm dusk plum instead of tech black, and the sage-green accent belongs exclusively to the sleep window, so green on any screen always means 'good time to try'.

baby-tracking-7.typography: SF Pro Rounded throughout, with the wake timer set in large soft numerals; rounded forms and generous sizes read at arm's length through half-closed eyes.
baby-tracking-7.motif: The green band: the sleep window is always drawn as one soft sage band on a horizontal day-line, identical on the main screen, the lock screen, and the history, so the whole product is legible as 'find the band'.

ia.coreObject: This baby's personal wake window, recalculated nightly from the last 5-7 days of real naps
ia.primaryLoop: Tap start when the baby sleeps, tap stop when they wake, glance at the lock screen for the next green band; parents return every nap, every day.

blood-pressure-log-2.territory: Two people use this at once: a 72-year-old holding a cuff and reading the screen at arm's length, and her daughter three time zones away who set it up and does not want another evening tech-support call. The interface answers with clinical calm scaled up: enormous numerals, one action per screen, and the unshakeable sameness of a well-printed medical form. Nothing moves, nothing surprises, nothing asks for a password.

palette.note: Pure white ground with near-black ink at maximum contrast; the medical blue marks only the save action and the active profile, and reading zones use muted green/amber fills wide enough that color is never the only signal.

blood-pressure-log-2.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything, readings set at 96pt with tabular figures; the typeface was designed for low vision, and here it simply gets to do its job at full size.
blood-pressure-log-2.motif: The three cells: systolic, diastolic and pulse always live in the same three giant fixed boxes in the same order on every screen, entry, history and summary alike, so the layout never has to be relearned.

calendars-tasks-1.territory: The user surfaces from two hours of hyperfocus with no idea what time it is and a low hum of dread about what they've missed. The tone hint's orderly confidence is right, but it must be confidence without judgment: daylight, clean grids, and a system that treats a blown plan as weather, not failure. The interface answers like a good external clock: it tells you where you are, what's next, and quietly rebuilds when the day breaks.

palette.note: A daylight-white field where the user's own block colors carry all the hue; cobalt marks only 'now' and system actions, so the current moment is always findable in one saccade.

calendars-tasks-1.typography: GT America for everything, with block labels set bold and hours set light; the grid types like a well-run train timetable, firm but never shouting.
calendars-tasks-1.motif: The open gap: unscheduled time is drawn as a first-class object, an airy dotted-edge slot with its length labeled ('45 min open'), so breathing room is visible before the day is overloaded, not after.

ia.coreObject: Today, as a column of color blocks and labeled open gaps

car-maintenance-8.territory: The landlord finishes a faucet run to the Maple Street duplex and wants the trip filed under the right roof before the next errand starts. The interface answers with clipboard competence: shop-floor plain, one-tap certain, and at tax time it hands over per-property numbers like a well-kept job book instead of one undifferentiated pile of miles.

palette.note: Flat shop-floor gray with white record cards; safety orange is reserved for untagged trips only, so the moment everything is filed the screen goes calm and colorless.

car-maintenance-8.typography: Archivo, condensed weights for table headers (DIN-flavored, work-order plain), with every mileage and dollar figure in tabular numerals so report columns land like a printed ledger.
car-maintenance-8.motif: The punched tag — every trip carries a key-tag-shaped chip with a punched hole, the same brass-tag silhouette as a garage pegboard; an untagged trip shows the empty punched outline in orange.

crypto-investing-1.territory: It is tax season and the user is about to sign their name under numbers they can't verify, after a year of tools that called moving their own money 'income'. The tone hint allows dark, but this territory demands the opposite: an accountant's daylight, ledger paper, ruled lines. The interface answers with clinical traceability, every figure looks like it can be pulled on and followed back to its source, because it can.

palette.note: Ledger-paper neutrals with a single bookkeeper's green for verified states and totals; nothing glows, nothing pulses, red appears only for genuine discrepancies.

crypto-investing-1.typography: IBM Plex Sans for labels and IBM Plex Mono for every number, right-aligned in columns; monospaced figures that always line up are the product's authority made visible.
crypto-investing-1.motif: The traceable underline: every computed number carries a fine dotted rule beneath it meaning 'this drills down to source transactions', and a number without the rule simply doesn't exist in the app.

ia.coreObject: A classified transaction (with its tax label, source record, and price at time of trade)
ia.primaryLoop: Once a season: connect sources, clear the review queue, drill a few numbers to build trust, export the report; the user returns when the queue has items or a new tax year opens.

dating-apps-2.territory: It is the small evening pocket when the couple finally checks in with each other, or across an ocean, when one of them is at breakfast and the other is winding down. The tone hint's chemistry and warmth translate here into anticipation: the pleasant suspense of a sealed answer you can't peek at. The interface answers with the intimacy of passed notes, warm light, soft paper, and a reveal that feels like opening something addressed only to you.

palette.note: Blush cream and warm white like late-afternoon light; the single ember-coral accent marks only moments of mutuality, the seal, the reveal, the pet's small heartbeat.

dating-apps-2.typography: GT Sectra for the daily question, set large like a letterpress prompt, with Graphik for answers and UI; the serif question and sans answers make the ritual feel authored, not generated.
dating-apps-2.motif: The sealed pair: every day is two facing cards, and the partner's card stays physically folded shut with a wax-dot seal until your own is sent, then both unfold in one synchronized motion.

ia.coreObject: Today's shared question and its two sealed answers
ia.primaryLoop: Answer the day's question, watch both cards unfold at once, leave one reaction; the sealed card waiting each evening and the growing pet bring both partners back daily.

driving-test-prep-7.territory: The person has a DMV appointment in nine days, a helmet on layaway, and a fresh memory of a prep app that quizzed them in kilometers about carburetors. The interface answers with the authority of American road signage itself: regulation shapes, regulation colors, calm drill rhythm, zero decoration. Confidence here comes from the material looking exactly like the world the exam tests.

palette.note: Concrete-gray ground with white question cards; MUTCD warning yellow appears only on charcoal sign-shaped chips and progress markers (never as text on white), so the accent always reads like signage, not UI candy.

driving-test-prep-7.typography: Overpass everywhere, the open typeface descended from Highway Gothic; questions set wide and unhurried, answers in the same voice as the signs they quote.
driving-test-prep-7.motif: Regulation silhouettes: every category, badge and progress marker lives inside an authentic MUTCD sign shape — diamond for hazards, pentagon for study, shield for your state, octagon only for hard stops.

ia.coreObject: A state-checked question bank drilled toward one exam date
ia.primaryLoop: A ten-minute drill a day: answer, read why it's right on a bike, watch weak diamonds turn solid, come back because the readiness shield inches toward your test date.

screens.purpose: The explanation mechanic earning its keep: two-wheel reasoning, not recycled car logic.

flashcards-5.territory: The person arrives protective and slightly tense: they are carrying years of study work in one file and they have been burned by importers before. The interface answers with the calm of a well-organized desk, showing every card face-up before anything is committed, so relief replaces suspicion within the first minute.

palette.note: Cards are warm manila objects on a cool gray desk, and the single ink-blue accent is reserved for the one action that commits data, so blue always means a decision.

flashcards-5.typography: Tiempos Text for card faces and headings, Inter for controls and metadata: the serif gives cards the gravity of printed study material while the sans keeps the machinery quiet.
flashcards-5.motif: The fanned five: every deck and every import is represented by five manila cards fanned like a hand you are allowed to inspect before you bet.

ia.coreObject: The deck, a portable stack that arrives whole and can leave whole
ia.primaryLoop: Review due cards each morning, watch intervals earned in Anki keep counting here, and bring in the next file whenever another course starts.

screens.title: Front door
screens.purpose: First launch opens directly on import, because the library is the reason anyone came.
screens.hero: A large drop zone drawn as an open manila folder with four format chips beneath it
screens.data: Chips: .apkg from Anki, CSV any encoding, delimited text, Quizlet set by link. Caption: Your intervals and review history travel with the cards. Secondary link: Start with an empty deck instead.

screens.title: Mapping desk
screens.purpose: Drag columns onto fields with a finger so any CSV shape becomes cards without documentation.

screens.data: Columns detected: A Term, B Definition, C System, D Mnemonic. A sits on Question, B on Answer, C on Tags, D unassigned with note: unassigned columns are kept in the card notes.

focus-productivity-1.territory: The user has been circling the same task for forty minutes, tabs multiplying, shame rising, because 25 minutes of imposed stillness has never once worked for them. The tone hint's calm workspace becomes something warmer: a fireside corner where someone is quietly making a thing while you make yours. The interface answers with companionable patience, ten honest minutes, sound without words, and a knitter who sets down her needles without a sigh when you have to go.

palette.note: Oat and undyed-wool neutrals with one heather-violet accent for the active sprint; the palette never brightens or flashes, because arousal is exactly what this user doesn't need.

focus-productivity-1.typography: Recoleta for headings with a soft mid-century roundness and Inter for UI; type feels like a well-set knitting pattern book, warm but precise.
focus-productivity-1.motif: The stitch row: time is rendered as rows of knit stitches accumulating on Wren's sock, one row per half-minute, so progress is fabric you can see growing rather than a countdown draining.

ia.coreObject: A sprint (5-20 minutes of sound, stitches, and one task)
ia.primaryLoop: Start a sprint, work while Wren knits and the sound holds, see the sock finished; the finished-object shelf and the app's learned 'your length is 12 minutes' bring the user back tomorrow.

screens.title: How long can you actually stay?
screens.purpose: Onboarding step one picks a starting sprint length and openly rejects the 25-minute default.
screens.hero: A length dial from 5 to 20 with a small honest caption under each stop
screens.data: Options: 5, 10 (selected, 'most people start here'), 15, 20. Copy: 'No 25/5. We'll learn which lengths you actually finish and adjust.' Button: 'Meet Wren'.

screens.title: This is Wren
screens.purpose: Onboarding step two introduces the character's contract and asks for the Live Activity honestly.
screens.hero: Wren in her chair, casting on, needles mid-loop
screens.data: Contract, three lines: 'She knits while you work. If you stop early, she sets her needles down and waits. She never guilt-trips.' Prompt: 'Show her on your lock screen during sprints?' Buttons: 'Yes, Live Activity', 'Not now'.

screens.title: Before the first row
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: the shelf is bare, the invitation is one small honest step.
screens.hero: An empty wooden shelf above Wren holding fresh yarn
screens.data: 'Nothing on the shelf yet.' Sub: 'Wren has cast on. Ten minutes makes the first sock.' Field: 'What are you working on? (optional)': 'draft the grant email'. Button: 'Start 10 minutes'.

screens.title: Mid-sprint
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: Wren knitting, rows accumulating, sound running, numbers kept quiet.
screens.hero: Wren knitting in rhythm, the sock at 13 of 24 rows, timer small in the corner
screens.data: Task chip: 'draft the grant email'. Rows: 13 of 24. Remaining: 5:30 of 12:00. Sound bar: 'Rain on wool, playing'. One control: 'Step away'. No pause-vs-quit interrogation.

screens.title: Sounds
screens.purpose: The wordless sound library, with the lock-screen persistence promise stated where it's chosen.
screens.hero: Four large fabric-textured tiles, one playing a live 10-second preview
screens.data: Tiles: 'Rain on wool' (playing), 'Loom room', 'Brown noise', 'Night train'. Footnote: 'Keeps playing with the screen locked and ducks under notifications instead of cutting out.' Mix: sound volume 70%, needle clicks 20% (off by default).

screens.title: Stepping away
screens.purpose: The early-exit state earning its keep: no penalty, no red, the work done so far stays real.
screens.hero: Wren setting her needles down in her lap, the half-sock resting on them
screens.data: 'She'll hold your row.' Sub: '7 of 12 minutes worked, and they count.' Buttons: 'Come back to it' , 'Done for now'. Nothing breaks, nothing resets, the partial rows appear in today's number.

screens.title: A finished sock
screens.purpose: Sprint completion: the object is done, the celebration is small and real, matched to the audience.
screens.hero: Wren holding up a finished heather sock, then setting it on the shelf
screens.data: '12 minutes. One sock.' Task chip: 'draft the grant email, done?' toggle. Buttons: 'One more sprint', 'That's the day'. Shelf count ticks: 47 objects since May.

screens.title: Your true length
screens.purpose: The learning mechanic shows its work: which sprint lengths this user actually finishes, and adjusts the default.
screens.hero: Four yarn skeins sized by completion rate, the 12-minute one fullest
screens.data: 'You finish 12-minute sprints 9 times out of 10. Twenty-minute ones, 1 in 5.' Change: 'Default set to 12 min. Twenty stays available, no judgment.' Based on: 63 sprints over 4 weeks. Button: 'Keep 12', 'Let me pick each time'.

screens.title: Lock screen
screens.purpose: The Live Activity keeps the sprint visible without unlocking the phone, the anti-doomscroll rail.
screens.hero: A lock-screen mock with a compact Wren, the row count, and time remaining
screens.data: Live Activity: 'Wren is knitting · row 13 of 24 · 5:30 left.' Dynamic Island collapsed: a tiny stitch glyph and 5:30. Tap does nothing but open the sprint, no feed, no badges.

screens.title: Today, one number
screens.purpose: The daily summary is a single figure, because dashboards are where this audience goes to feel bad.
screens.hero: One large numeral over a small row of today's socks
screens.data: '5 sprints.' Beneath, small: '58 minutes, longest 15.' No streak, no week-over-week arrow, no red days. Yesterday is one swipe away and looks identical.

screens.title: Yarn money

food-delivery-3.territory: The person is hungry and wary at the same time: they are about to hand their health to a stranger's kitchen through a comment field, and last time the note was ignored. The interface answers with the calm of a well-run allergy clinic that also loves food: bright daylight, appetizing but honest photography, and every safety claim traced to a named source. Appetite stays, dread leaves.

palette.note: Green is spent only on verified-safe states, amber #C77B1F only on watch-list warnings, so color itself reads as a safety verdict and never as decoration.

food-delivery-3.typography: Söhne for UI and National 2 Condensed for chain names, with the order instruction card set in IBM Plex Mono like a real kitchen chit; the type sounds like a competent expeditor, not a cheery mascot.
food-delivery-3.motif: The kitchen chit: every safe order condenses into a perforated ticket-shaped card with tear-line edges, the exact artifact that travels from the app into the restaurant's comment field.

ia.coreObject: A verified menu item at a specific chain, scored against the user's restriction profile
ia.primaryLoop: Before every food order the user opens their chain, checks what is safe today for their profile, copies the instruction chit into the delivery app, and afterwards reports whether the note reached the kitchen, which feeds everyone else's map.

habit-tracking-6.territory: The coach is ten minutes out from a session, coffee in hand, needing instant command of a client's last two weeks without scrolling through screenshots and texts. The interface answers with crisp, rhythmic order: everything already tallied, the week laid out like woven fabric, small wins visibly compounding into a pattern the coach can read at a glance and quote out loud.

palette.note: Cobalt marks completion cells and nothing else; misses are honest pale gray, never red, because the report goes in front of a client and shame is not the methodology.

habit-tracking-6.typography: Untitled Sans with strictly tabular figures for every count and percentage, Tiempos Headline only for client names on reports; the type reads like a well-set practice document, quietly authoritative.

intermittent-fasting-6.territory: A night-shift nurse ends her last meal at 3 a.m. and every fasting app tells her she is doing it wrong. The interface answers with calm discipline unhooked from the wall clock: warm bone paper, a dial with no 12 o'clock, and hours that accumulate from wherever she actually started. Her schedule is treated as the norm, not the exception.

palette.note: The dusk-lavender arc deepens gradually with elapsed hours, and nothing on screen is ever colored by clock time: color answers only 'how long', never 'how late'.

intermittent-fasting-6.typography: Newsreader carries the calm sentences in a bookish serif while Inter with tabular figures does the hour math; numbers read like a quiet ledger, not a scoreboard.
intermittent-fasting-6.motif: The unclocked dial: a ring with no 12 o'clock and no tick marks, whose zero sits wherever you started; hours accumulate along the arc like a moon phase, indifferent to the wall clock.

ia.coreObject: The fast: a duration anchored to a real start point, not a clock time
ia.primaryLoop: Tap start when the last meal actually ends, watch hours accumulate, close the fast; the saved week template queues the next one by itself.

invoice-maker-2.territory: The contractor is between jobs sites, phone in a dusty hand, wanting to look like a real business and not lose a client to a confusing deposit ask. The interface answers with daylight paperwork calm: everything reads like a clean printed estimate, both parties always see the same numbers, and money questions answer themselves.

palette.note: Ledger green appears only where money has actually moved, paid amounts and unlocked payment buttons, so a glance at any screen shows the true payment state.

invoice-maker-2.typography: IBM Plex Serif for document headers and totals, IBM Plex Sans with tabular figures for line items: the pairing reads like well-set business paper, and every number column aligns to the cent.
invoice-maker-2.motif: The perforation: a tear-line across every job document separating the deposit from the balance, which visibly seals itself green as each half is paid.

journaling-mood-8.territory: The person opens the app at 11:40 pm, two weeks after their last entry, braced for the app to make them feel like a quitter again. The interface answers with the warmth of a paper notebook that simply has some blank pages: cream, ink, a serif that talks like a kind friend, and a calendar that treats gaps as weather, not failure. Twenty seconds later they're done and nothing scolded them.

palette.note: Terracotta appears only where the user leaves a mark, like ink from one pen; empty days stay the same cream as the page, deliberately indistinguishable from rest.

journaling-mood-8.typography: Tiempos Text carries all reflective copy in a warm serif voice while söhne-style Atkinson Hyperlegible handles labels and buttons; icons are chunky enough to feel like rubber stamps, not UI glyphs.
journaling-mood-8.motif: The rubber stamp: every logged day is a small cluster of inked stamp icons pressed onto cream paper with slight rotation and ink-texture, so a filled month looks like a well-used passport, and a gap is just clean paper.

ia.coreObject: A day, marked with mood and stamp icons, optionally one line of text
ia.primaryLoop: Whenever the person remembers, today or three weeks later, they stamp a day in about twenty seconds; the total-entries counter ticks up regardless of gaps, and search lets them ask their own history what was going on.

screens.data: June: 14 stamped days, an unbroken blank stretch Jun 8–16. Caption under the grid, serif: '14 entries in June. The quiet week is just a quiet week.' Tap target on any blank day: 'Fill this day in'.

screens.title: Fill in June 12
screens.purpose: Retroactive logging with photo-library memory prompts, the mechanic that makes gaps repairable.
screens.hero: A horizontal strip of the user's own photos from that date above the standard stamp grid.
screens.data: Photos from Jun 12: a birthday cake, a rainy bus window, a screenshot of a text thread. Prompt: 'Your camera says June 12 had cake.' User stamps: 'celebration', 'rain', mood face four. Line added: 'Dad's 60th'. Note: 'Photos stay on your phone. We only look at dates.'

screens.title: Find · 'what was March'
screens.purpose: Search by stamps and words, the answer to the core ADHD-memory question.
screens.hero: A search bar with stamp-chips as filters and results as a river of dated entry cards.
screens.data: Query: stamp 'slept badly' + word 'meds'. Results: 'Mar 4 — slept badly, deadline — «new meds day 3, wired»', 'Mar 11 — slept badly — «skipped dose?»', 'May 2 — slept badly, walked'. Summary line: '9 matches across 7 months'.

screens.title: Your totals
screens.purpose: The stats page rebuilt around accumulation instead of chains.
screens.hero: One huge serif number: total entries, with stamp-frequency rows beneath.
screens.data: '83 entries since November.' Most-used stamps: walked ×31, slept badly ×24, saw Ana ×12. Gentle pattern line: '«slept badly» shows up twice as often in weeks with «deadline».' Explicitly absent: any longest-streak figure.

screens.title: One entry, reread
screens.purpose: Entry detail: the moment months later when a stamped day becomes a memory.
screens.hero: The day's stamps rendered large at the top like a passport page, the one line beneath in serif, photos from that date below.
screens.data: 'Feb 14 · mood 4 · celebration, cooked, saw Ana · «made the ramen from the video, it actually worked».' Footer actions: edit stamps, add a line, 'Copy date link'.

screens.title: First open, blank book
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: a notebook with nothing in it should feel inviting, not broken.
screens.hero: The Today screen with the stamp grid fully visible and touchable, and a single serif caption.
screens.data: Caption above the grid: 'This page is today. Tap anything.' The Pages tab shows the current month completely cream with: 'Months fill up from whatever day you start. Backfilling counts too.'

screens.title: Late-night ink
screens.purpose: Night mode for the 11:40 pm check-in, since most entries happen in bed.
screens.hero: The Today screen re-papered: deep brown-black page, cream ink, terracotta unchanged, stamps glowing softly like embers.
screens.data: Same entry flow at reduced brightness; system schedule chip: 'Night paper: sunset to sunrise'. Mood faces keep their shapes, colors drop saturation. Footer: 'Everything else works the same in the dark.'

screens.title: Buy it once
screens.purpose: The paywall: a one-time price pitched to an audience burned by subscriptions, with the free tier stated first.
screens.hero: A single price tag rendered as a stamped cream card, no plan grid, no timer.
screens.data: Header: 'Free forever: mood + 8 stamps, full calendar, backfill.' Offer: 'Everything, once — $11.99. All stamp sets, photo prompts, search by words, night paper, export.' One serif line: 'No subscription. You were promised that on screen one.' Links, equally weighted: 'Restore purchase' · 'What exactly is paid?'

screens.title: Your data leaves with you
screens.purpose: Export and backup, because a journal that can be lost is a journal that won't be trusted.
screens.hero: Two large cards: 'Export everything' and 'Automatic backup'.
screens.data: Export: 'PDF (looks like these pages) or CSV — 83 entries, 1.2 MB'. Backup: 'iCloud, encrypted, last backup today 07:12'. Note: 'No account, no server of ours. Delete the app and the export is still yours.'

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Quiet controls: stamps, reminders that ask instead of nag, and privacy.
screens.hero: Grouped cream list with the custom stamp editor on top.
screens.data: My stamps: edit set (add 'physio', archive 'gym'). Reminder: 'One gentle nudge, 9:30 pm, wording: «Want to stamp today? Fine if not.» — on'. Privacy: Face ID lock — on; photo access — 'dates only, granted'. Night paper: automatic.

language-learning-1.territory: The person has just spent ten minutes speaking a foreign language out loud and feels the specific vulnerability of having been heard making mistakes. The interface answers like a rigorous, good-humored coach at the whiteboard: bright, energetic, zero fluff praise, everything pointed at the three concrete things to fix. The mood is a training gym for speech where crossing an error off the list feels like racking a heavier weight.

palette.note: Coral-red is the teacher's pen and marks only open errors; when an error closes it is overstruck in deep green #1F7A4D, so the palette narrates the loop from caught to cured.

language-learning-1.typography: ABC Favorit for UI with its slightly athletic geometry, and Martina Plantijn italic reserved for corrected phrasings in the transcript, so the 'right way to say it' literally reads in a different voice.
language-learning-1.motif: The margin mark: every transcript carries a live left margin where coral pen strokes appear beside stumbles, exactly like a returned essay, and a closed error gets the same stroke in green with a single strike-through.

ia.coreObject: A recurring error: a specific rule you break, with its history and its status (open or closed)
ia.primaryLoop: Ten minutes of spoken dialogue on a chosen topic, then the breakdown of three stumbles; tomorrow's dialogue is engineered to resurface open errors until each one is closed, and closed errors are the only score that moves.

screens.title: Say something
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: a 60-second voice sample instead of a level quiz, because the app grades speech, not multiple choice.
screens.hero: A single prompt card with a large record button and a live waveform.
screens.data: Prompt: 'Describe your last trip, in German, for one minute. Mistakes wanted — that's the material.' After recording: 'Heard: solid B1 base, article errors, verb-final word order slips. Good. We can work with this.'

screens.title: What do you want to talk about?
screens.purpose: Second onboarding step: pick real topics so dialogues never feel like filler chat.
screens.hero: Topic tiles with honest, adult subjects.
screens.data: Selected: 'Work meetings', 'Negotiating rent', 'Small talk I actually need'. Skipped: 'Ordering food'. Footer: 'The AI won't pretend to be your friend. Ten minutes, your topic, then the breakdown.'

screens.title: Live dialogue · Rent negotiation
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: mid-conversation, speech-first, the margin quietly collecting material.
screens.hero: A tall transcript with the AI's last line and the user's response being transcribed live, margin strip visible on the left.
screens.data: AI: 'Die Wohnung kostet 1.400 € warm. Was schlagen Sie vor?' User (transcribing): 'Ich denke, dass der Preis ist zu hoch…' — a faint coral tick appears in the margin, unlabeled. Timer: 6:12 / 10:00. One button: 'Wrap up'.

screens.title: The breakdown
screens.purpose: Post-dialogue analysis: exactly three stumbles, each with the rule and the correct phrasing, nothing padded.
screens.hero: Three margin-marked cards stacked, each pairing your line with the corrected line in italic.
screens.data: 1. You said: 'dass der Preis ist zu hoch' → Rule: verb goes last in dass-clauses → 'dass der Preis zu hoch ist'. 2. 'mit dem Vermieter sprechen über' → separable framing → 'mit dem Vermieter darüber sprechen'. 3. Article: 'das Miete' → die Miete (fem.). Footer: 'Stumble #1 has now appeared 3 times — added to My Errors.'

screens.title: My Errors
screens.purpose: The personal recurring-error list, the product's actual scoreboard.
screens.hero: A ledger of open errors in coral and closed ones struck through in green.
screens.data: Open: 'Verb-final in dass-clauses — seen 4×, last today', 'die/das Miete — 3×', 'Adjective endings after ein — 6×, oldest open (since May 12)'. Closed this month: 'wenn vs. als — closed Jun 21 after 5 clean uses'. Header: '3 open · 11 closed all-time'.

screens.title: It came back
screens.purpose: The resurfacing moment mid-dialogue: yesterday's error re-enters in a fresh context and the user nails it.
screens.hero: The live transcript with a margin mark flipping from coral outline to solid green as the clean sentence lands.
screens.data: AI steers: 'Warum glauben Sie, dass die Nebenkosten fair sind?' User: '…weil ich denke, dass der Betrag angemessen ist.' Inline chip: 'dass-clause: clean use 2 of 5'. Nothing celebratory beyond the chip — the gym doesn't applaud every rep.

screens.title: Hands-free · driving
screens.purpose: Car mode: start with voice, finish with voice, breakdown deferred to the screen later.
screens.hero: A near-black high-contrast screen with one giant waveform and enormous type, nothing tappable below the fold.
screens.data: 'Say «start» to begin · Topic: Work meetings (yesterday's open errors loaded)'. During: only elapsed time '4:51' in 96 pt. End line spoken by the app: 'Done. Two stumbles saved. Breakdown is waiting on your screen.'

screens.title: Progress = errors closed
screens.purpose: The stats page that replaces streaks with the only counter the product believes in.
screens.hero: A big paired figure: closed vs. open, with a monthly closing-rate bar chart underneath.
screens.data: '11 closed · 3 open.' June: 4 closed, 9 dialogues, 92 spoken minutes. Longest-open callout: 'Adjective endings after ein — open 51 days. Next dialogue will lean on it.' No day-streak anywhere.

screens.title: Take it to your tutor
screens.purpose: Export: one file with the full dialogue and breakdown, built to hand to a human teacher.
screens.hero: A document preview combining transcript, margin marks, and the error ledger delta.
screens.data: File: 'Rent negotiation — Jul 2 — 10 min.pdf'. Contents listed: full transcript with margin marks, 3 stumbles with rules, error list snapshot. Share targets: email, WhatsApp, AirDrop. Note: 'Tutors tell us this saves the first 15 minutes of a lesson.'

screens.title: Empty gym
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state after onboarding: no dialogues yet, the ledger unmissably blank.
screens.hero: The My Errors ledger rendered with empty ruled lines like a fresh notebook page.
screens.data: Copy: 'Your error list is empty because we haven't heard you yet. It won't stay empty — that's the point.' Button: 'First dialogue · 10 min · Rent negotiation'. Sub-line: 'Your onboarding sample already suggested two candidates.'

screens.title: The math against a tutor
screens.purpose: The paywall: priced honestly against the human alternative the user is already comparing.
screens.hero: A two-column comparison card, tutor hour vs. month of the app, followed by one plan.
screens.data: Left: 'Human tutor: $35–60 / hour.' Right: 'Unlimited dialogues + error tracking: $17.99 / month or $119 / year.' Free tier stated: '2 dialogues a week free, breakdowns included, error list capped at 3.' Trial: '7 days full access, reminder the day before it ends.' Footer links, same size: 'Restore purchase' · 'Cancel anytime, it's one tap in Settings'.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Control over language, correction intensity, audio behavior, and data.
screens.hero: Grouped list with the correction-style control on top, since it defines the relationship.
screens.data: Language: German (B1) · add another. Correction style: 'Strict (mark everything recurring)' vs 'Top 3 only' — Top 3 selected. Voice: speaking speed 0.9×. Car mode: auto-start on CarPlay — on. Data: 'Export all transcripts', 'Delete voice recordings after breakdown — on'. Subscription: monthly · Manage · Restore purchase.

meal-prep-grocery-4.territory: The person is mid-errand with one hand on a cart, mildly annoyed at the idea of backtracking to aisle 3 for the milk they walked past. The interface answers with the calm of a well-kept paper list that happens to know the building: no map, no retailer branding, just your items in the order your feet already go. It should feel like the list was written by a slightly more organized version of you.

palette.note: Warm paper background with white list cards; the market green appears only on the route thread, checkmarks and the learning meter, so color always means 'the route is at work'.

meal-prep-grocery-4.typography: Karla for headers and store names, Inter with tabular figures for the list itself; type stays checklist-plain and lowercase-friendly, like a grocery list written by someone tidy.
meal-prep-grocery-4.motif: The route thread: a single continuous green line that stitches section headers together in your walk order, drawn dashed while the app is still learning and turning solid trip by trip.

ia.coreObject: A per-store list whose section order is a learned route
ia.primaryLoop: Before the trip you dump items in any order, in the store you check them off top to bottom without backtracking, and each checkoff quietly teaches the route for next week.

screens.title: Onboarding · Your stores
screens.purpose: Collect the 1-3 stores the person actually shops weekly, nothing else.
screens.hero: A short store list being built with an add field on top
screens.data: Added: 'Trader Joe's — Capitol Hill', 'Costco — 4th Ave S'. Search field placeholder: 'Safeway, WinCo, H-E-B…'. Footnote: 'Each store gets its own route. You can add more later.'

screens.title: Onboarding · Shop like you always do
screens.purpose: Set the one expectation that makes the product work: no setup, the route builds itself.
screens.hero: A dashed route thread connecting three ghost sections, with 'trip 1 · trip 2 · trip 3' ticks along it
screens.data: Headline: 'Three trips. That's the whole setup.' Body: 'Shop in your usual order and check things off. By trip three, your list sorts itself to match your path. Works fully offline in the store.' Button: 'Start my first list'.

screens.title: First list (empty state)
screens.purpose: Get the first items in before the first trip, with the learning meter honest at zero.
screens.hero: An empty white list card with a big add field and a dashed, faint route thread
screens.data: Store chip: 'Trader Joe's — Capitol Hill'. Meter: 'Route: trip 0 of 3'. Placeholder rows: 'Try: milk, bananas, coffee'. Hint: 'Type or paste your whole list. Order doesn't matter yet — that's my job.'

screens.title: List mid-shop, trip 3
screens.purpose: The main screen at the moment the product proves itself: half-checked list already roughly in walk order.
screens.hero: The list with the route thread now mostly solid, checked items collapsing upward
screens.data: Meter: 'Trip 3 of 3 — route ready after today'. Sections in learned order: Produce (bananas ✓, cilantro ✓, 2 avocados), Bakery (sourdough ✓), Frozen (gyoza, mango chunks), Dairy — last (whole milk, greek yogurt). 11 items, 4 done. Offline dot: 'no signal, all good'.

screens.title: Route ready
screens.purpose: Celebrate quietly and show exactly what was learned, because the route is the paid-for asset.
screens.hero: The thread animating from dashed to solid down a compact section-order card
screens.data: Headline: 'Your Trader Joe's route is ready.' Learned order: 1 Produce, 2 Bakery, 3 Pantry, 4 Frozen, 5 Snacks, 6 Dairy. Note: 'Milk kept landing last across 3 trips, so Dairy sits at the bottom.' Button: 'Looks right' / link: 'Fix something'.

screens.title: Store switcher
screens.purpose: One tap between stores, each with its own visibly different route.
screens.hero: Two store cards side by side, each with its own miniature thread shape
screens.data: 'Trader Joe's — Capitol Hill · route solid · 14 trips' with order Produce→Dairy; 'Costco — 4th Ave S · route solid · 6 trips' with order Pharmacy→Produce→Freezer→Checkout snacks. Button: '+ Add a store'.

screens.title: Drag to reorder
screens.purpose: Manual correction that coexists with learning instead of fighting it.
screens.hero: A section row lifted mid-drag with the thread bending elastically around it
screens.data: Dragging 'Frozen' from position 4 to 5. Toast after drop: 'Frozen moved after Snacks. I'll keep refining from your checkoffs — this stays unless your trips say otherwise.'

screens.title: Next two aisles
screens.purpose: The in-store focus mode: only what you are grabbing right now, readable at arm's length over a cart.
screens.hero: Two oversized section blocks filling the whole screen, everything else gone
screens.data: Now — Pantry: 'olive oil, jasmine rice 2 lb, canned chickpeas ×3'. Next — Frozen: 'gyoza, mango chunks'. Progress footer: '7 of 11 · Dairy is last, as usual'. Swipe hint: 'swipe up when your hands are done here'.

screens.title: Route change confirmation
screens.purpose: Honor the no-silent-reshuffle promise: the app proposes, the owner decides.
screens.hero: A before/after order card with one section highlighted for the move
screens.data: Headline: 'Your last 3 trips look different.' Body: 'You've been grabbing Bakery right after Frozen lately. Move Bakery from #2 to #5?' Buttons: 'Yes, update my route' / 'No, keep my order'. Footnote: 'I never reshuffle a learned route without asking.'

screens.title: In-store, offline
screens.purpose: Show that dead-zone concrete-walled stores change nothing.
screens.hero: The normal mid-shop list with a small quiet 'offline' pebble in the header, zero degradation
screens.data: Banner (footnote-sized, not a warning): 'No connection — list, route and checkoffs all live on this phone. Sync resumes at home.' List continues: Snacks (tortilla chips ✓, dark chocolate).

screens.title: Route export & backup
screens.purpose: Make ownership tangible: the route is a file you can hold and move.
screens.hero: A route card rendered like a boarding pass with an export arrow
screens.data: 'Trader Joe's — Capitol Hill · 6 sections · learned over 14 trips · last refined Jun 28'. Buttons: 'Back up to cloud (Plus)', 'Export file (.route)'. Line: 'Restoring on a new phone takes one import. No account needed for export.'

screens.title: Paywall · Keep the route safe
screens.purpose: Sell continuity, not features: the route took weeks to learn and should never be lost.
screens.hero: The solid route thread coiled into a small knot icon above two plain price cards
screens.data: Headline: 'You built this route over 14 trips.' Card 1: 'App, one store, forever — $2.99 one-time'. Card 2: 'Plus — $10/year: unlimited stores, cloud backup, automatic new-phone restore'. Footnote: 'No trial tricks. Everything you've learned stays yours either way.' Link: 'Restore purchase'.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Few controls, all about ownership and learning behavior.
screens.hero: A short grouped list, paper background, no icons carnival
screens.data: Learning: 'Ask before changing a learned route — On', 'Trips needed to learn — 3'. Data: 'Export all routes', 'Cloud backup — Plus', 'Delete a store profile'. Display: 'Collapse checked items — On'. About: 'Version 1.4 · your lists never leave this phone unless you back them up'.

meditation-mindfulness-9.territory: The person arrives with a mind going ninety miles an hour and a history of failing at 'sit still and close your eyes', half-expecting this app to fail them the same way. The interface answers with dusk: enormous quiet space, one softly lit point to hold onto, almost no UI at all. Not the fake serenity of a spa, but the specific relief of finally being given something to do with your attention.

palette.note: One warm amber point of light on a plum dusk, no gradients screaming for attention; in the morning set the whole palette inverts to a pale dawn #F1EDE7 with the same single amber anchor, because a wired 8 am brain needs different light than a winding-down one.

meditation-mindfulness-9.typography: Suisse Int'l Light with generous tracking for the few words that exist, and no display face at all; instructions appear one short line at a time, sized large, because reading is also an attention task here.
meditation-mindfulness-9.motif: The anchor point: a single slow-drifting amber dot that opens every session and behaves differently per practice — it flows in the visual stream, pulses with your step rhythm on walks, and rests in the corner during hands-on work, always the one thing the eye can come home to.

ia.coreObject: A session with a physical anchor: eyes, hands, steps, or sound
ia.primaryLoop: Two or three times a day, at the wired morning or the frayed evening, the person picks an anchor and gives it 3–7 minutes; nothing counts consecutive days, so returning after a week feels identical to returning after an hour.

screens.title: Pick what holds you
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: choose a starting anchor by feel, not by questionnaire.
screens.hero: Four large tactile tiles, each already faintly animating its anchor: a drifting stream, hands, footsteps, sound bars.
screens.data: Tiles: 'Eyes — watch a stream', 'Hands — color and touch', 'Steps — walk it off', 'Sound — layer noise under work'. Selected: Steps. One line beneath: 'No session here asks you to sit still with your eyes closed. Ever.'

screens.title: When is your brain loudest?
screens.purpose: Second onboarding step: set the day/night split so the app offers the right set at the right hour.
screens.hero: A single horizontal dusk-to-dawn slider with two markers.
screens.data: Markers placed: 'Wired — 8:00–10:00 am', 'Fried — after 9:30 pm'. Result line: 'Mornings we'll offer steps and sound. Nights, the stream and hands. You can ignore all of this.'

screens.title: Now · 9:47 pm
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: the night set, three sessions, nothing else on screen.
screens.hero: Enormous empty plum space with the amber anchor dot resting center, three session rows floating low.
screens.data: 'Stream · 5 min — slow field with voice'. 'Hands · 7 min — coloring: harbor at night'. 'Body scan you can fidget through · 4 min'. Top corner, small: 'Night set'. No streak, no ring, no greeting.

screens.title: The stream, minute two
screens.purpose: The visual-anchor session at its earning-its-keep moment: eyes open, attention held by motion.
screens.hero: A full-bleed, slow particle stream flowing diagonally, the amber dot riding it; UI reduced to one word.
screens.data: Voice line rendered as caption: 'When you notice you've left, find the amber dot. That's the whole practice.' Remaining: a hairline arc, no numerals. Single control on tap: 'End softly' (30-second fade).

screens.title: Walk it off
screens.purpose: The walking practice start screen: phone goes in the pocket, the practice follows your actual step rhythm.
screens.hero: The anchor dot pulsing at the cadence detected from the first few steps, above one oversized button.
screens.data: 'Detected: ~104 steps/min. Voice will land on your rhythm, not a metronome.' Button: 'Pocket the phone to begin'. Sub-line: '6 min · eyes open · ends with three slower breaths, still walking.' Lock screen Live Activity preview: amber dot + '4:12 left'.

screens.title: Hands on · Harbor at night
screens.purpose: The interactive coloring session with body-awareness audio, the hands anchor at work.
screens.hero: A line-art harbor being filled with a fingertip, color pooling like watercolor; the anchor dot rests in a corner.
screens.data: Audio caption: 'As you fill the water, notice the weight of the phone in your other hand.' Progress: 'Region 4 of 9'. No undo button by design; a small note in first use: 'Uneven color is the point.'

screens.title: Sound under work
screens.purpose: The layered-noise focus mode for tasks, the fourth anchor, running behind other apps.
screens.hero: Three horizontal layer sliders as thin amber lines on dusk: texture, low tone, room.
screens.data: Layers set: rain texture 60%, brown tone 40%, café room 15%. Timer: 'Until I stop it' selected over 25/45 min presets. Line: 'Keeps playing under a locked screen and through notifications.'

screens.title: That was 6 minutes
screens.purpose: Session end: acknowledgment without score, the anti-streak position made tangible.
screens.hero: The anchor dot settling to stillness in the center as the stream fades, one line of text.
screens.data: 'Walked 6 minutes. 642 steps held the line.' Below, quiet: 'Nothing to keep up. Come back whenever it's loud again.' Two ghost buttons: 'Again, shorter' · 'Done'.

screens.title: Dawn set
screens.purpose: The morning variant: the palette inverts to pale daylight because the wired brain needs a different room.
screens.hero: The Now screen re-lit: warm paper #F1EDE7 background, ink text, the same amber dot now a spot of sun.
screens.data: 'Morning set · 8:12 am'. Sessions: 'Steps · 5 min — out the door version', 'Sound · until you stop — work start', 'Stream · 3 min — fast field (yes, fast)'. Corner toggle: 'Dusk / Dawn — automatic'.

screens.title: Nothing here yet, on purpose
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state on the You tab: history absent without implying failure.
screens.hero: A dark field with a single unlit dot and one sentence.
screens.data: 'Sessions you finish will glow here as dots — a pile, not a chain. Gaps will never be marked.' Button: 'Try the 3-minute stream now'.

screens.title: A week to prove it
screens.purpose: The paywall: full-access trial first because this audience has been burned by meditation apps before, price stated plainly in the same quiet voice.
screens.hero: One dusk card with the amber dot above a single yearly price, no plan grid, no timer animation.
screens.data: 'Everything free for 7 days. Then $54.99 / year — all anchors, all sets, offline packs.' Context line: 'About what Loona or Mesmerize costs. Cancel during the trial and you pay nothing, we'll remind you on day 6.' Links, equal weight: 'Restore purchase' · 'Keep only the free daily stream' (3-min stream stays free forever).

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The few controls this product allows, plus honest data and audio behavior.
screens.hero: A short grouped list, dusk-surfaced, with the set schedule on top.
screens.data: Sets: Dawn 6–11 am, Dusk after 8 pm, automatic. Voice: 'Fewer words' — on. Haptics on walk cadence — on. Downloads: 'Night pack, 84 MB — saved for offline'. Health: 'Read step cadence from motion sensor only, never location'. Subscription: trial, day 3 · Manage · Restore purchase.

messaging-apps-4.territory: The practitioner has watched colleagues lose a decade of client history to an unappealable platform ban, and every WhatsApp ping from a client now carries a low hum of professional risk. The interface answers with the airy composure of good stationery: light, fast, human in tone, and structurally reassuring, everything visibly on the practitioner's own letterhead, under their own key, on their own link.

palette.note: Deep petrol green is the color of ownership: it draws the letterhead rule, the encryption badge, and send actions, while everything conversational stays in warm neutrals so threads read like correspondence, not chat bubbles in a toy.

messaging-apps-4.typography: Signifier for the practice name and letterhead lines, giving every screen the gravity of engraved stationery, with Inter handling messages and UI at speed; timestamps and receipt states in small caps.
messaging-apps-4.motif: The letterhead rule: a fine double hairline under the practice name crowns every screen, thread, exported PDF, and the client's browser view, the same mark everywhere, the visual proof that this channel belongs to the practitioner and travels with them.

ia.coreObject: A client thread living on its own unique practitioner-issued link
ia.primaryLoop: Clients write through their personal browser link at all hours; the practitioner answers within office hours, and every exchange lands in a searchable, exportable archive that no platform can revoke.

screens.title: Your letterhead
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: establish the practice identity that will crown every screen and export.
screens.hero: A live letterhead preview, double hairline drawing itself under the name as the practitioner types.
screens.data: Fields: 'R. Calloway, CPA' · 'Tax & small business accounting'. Link preview: 'calloway.channel/…'. Line beneath: 'This page is yours. It stays up as long as you pay, and leaves with you if you go.'

screens.title: Office hours, honestly
screens.purpose: Second onboarding step: set the hours so clients see a truthful response window instead of silence.
screens.hero: A weekly grid with draggable hour bands and a preview of what the client will read outside them.
screens.data: Set: Mon–Fri 9:00–17:30. Client-side preview: 'R. Calloway typically replies within office hours (Mon–Fri 9–5:30 ET). Your message is delivered and saved.' Toggle: 'Urgent keyword alert ("audit", "deadline") — on'.

screens.title: Inbox · Tuesday 9:04
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: the morning triage of client threads at the start of office hours.
screens.hero: Thread rows under the letterhead, each with client name, last line, and receipt state in small caps.
screens.data: 'M. Okafor — «attached the Q2 payroll summary» · DELIVERED 8:12'. 'Hendricks LLC — «can we move Thursday?» · READ BY YOU'. 'D. Reyes — «signed copy came back from the bank» · NEW'. Header: '3 awaiting reply · office hours open 8h 26m'.

screens.title: Thread · M. Okafor
screens.purpose: The conversation view: one-on-one correspondence with receipts that track commitments.
screens.hero: A calm two-column-margined thread, practitioner messages on letterhead-white, encryption badge fixed in the header.
screens.data: Client, 8:12: 'Attached the Q2 payroll summary — is the contractor line where you expected?' + payroll-Q2.pdf (1.4 MB). Practitioner draft in composer: 'Line 7 looks right. I'll file the amendment before Friday —'. Header badge: 'End-to-end encrypted · archive on your side'. Receipt under last client message: DELIVERED 8:12 · READ 9:06.

mind-mapping-6.territory: A med student at 11pm, three days out from an exam, holding a dense lecture that keeps slipping out of shape. The interface answers with airy, playful precision: a wide-open canvas that makes heavy material feel arrangeable, and a self-test mode that feels like turning cards face-down on a table you built yourself, not an interrogation.

palette.note: The canvas stays chalk-white so the student's own node colors carry the map; recall coral appears only on things that ask for memory — veiled nodes, due reviews, blanked marks.

mind-mapping-6.typography: Space Grotesk for node labels and headings, Inter for UI, STIX Two Math for formulas; the slightly squared grotesk makes hand-arranged maps look deliberate rather than messy.
mind-mapping-6.motif: The veiled node — a frosted-glass pill that hides a branch label while keeping its exact position and silhouette, turning the map into its own deck of face-down cards.

ia.coreObject: the map (a lecture rebuilt as positioned nodes)
ia.primaryLoop: Build tonight's lecture into the map, flip a branch face-down before bed, and come back when the review queue says a forgotten node is due.

screens.title: Position is the cue
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: teach the single belief the app runs on before asking for anything.
screens.hero: A small live map where one node fades to frost and reappears in the exact same spot as the copy explains why place equals memory.
screens.data: Mini map titled 'Cardiac cycle' with nodes Systole, Diastole, SA node; caption: 'You remember the answer because you remember where it sat.'

screens.title: Build, veil, recall
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: show the three-beat loop in one animation, then get out of the way.
screens.hero: A branch of four nodes flipping face-down in sequence, then one being uncovered by a thumb.
screens.data: Three captions: '1. Map the lecture · 2. Veil a branch · 3. Uncover from memory'; single button 'Start your first map'.

screens.title: Blank canvas
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state that makes the intimidating white page feel like a starting move.
screens.hero: One lonely starter node in the canvas center with a pulsing plus handle.
screens.data: Starter node reads 'Lecture 1 — rename me'; ghost hints: 'drag to branch', 'double-tap for a formula'; secondary action 'Import an outline (.txt, .opml)'.

screens.title: Canvas mid-lecture
screens.purpose: The main screen with a real map in progress, dense but fast.
screens.hero: A 47-node map with three color-coded branches and a photo peeking out of one node.
screens.data: Map 'Cardiac Cycle — Lecture 12'; branches: Electrical conduction (SA node 60–100 bpm, AV node delay 0.09 s), Pressure curves, Heart sounds (S1 = mitral + tricuspid closure); node with formula CO = HR × SV; footer: '47 nodes · saved just now'.

screens.title: Inside a node

screens.hero: An expanded node card with a rendered formula above a cropped lecture-slide photo.
screens.data: Node 'Stroke volume'; formula SV = EDV − ESV; values EDV 120 mL, ESV 50 mL; photo captioned 'slide 23, Wiggers diagram'; label chips: Cardio, High-yield.

screens.title: Filter by label

screens.data: Chips: Cardio, Renal, High-yield, 'Prof said exam'; active: High-yield; status line 'Showing 18 of 47 nodes'.

screens.title: Self-test: branch veiled

screens.data: Testing branch 'Electrical conduction'; progress '6 of 9 recalled'; per-node buttons 'Got it' / 'Blanked'; just-revealed node: 'AV node delay 0.09 s'.

screens.title: What you blanked on

screens.hero: Three coral nodes lifted off the map into a short stack with return dates.
screens.data: '3 nodes blanked: AV node delay · Bundle of His · S3 gallop'; schedule: 'back tomorrow, then in 4 days, then in 7'; button 'Done for tonight'.

music-streaming-1.territory: The listener knows exactly what they want to hear tonight, the Eroica, and the delicious question is only whose. The interface answers like the lobby of a concert hall at eight o'clock: dark, hushed, warm brass light on ivory type, the programme in your hands. It treats choosing between Karajan and Kleiber as the main event, and then steps aside to let someone else's streaming service do the playing.

palette.note: Warm charcoal, never blue-black, with brass reserved for the listener's own marks — ratings, diary entries, editorial laurels — so the user's taste literally gilds the catalog over time.

music-streaming-1.typography: Canela in its light cuts for work titles and composer names, set like a printed programme, with Founders Grotesk for the dense recording metadata; opus numbers and years in tabular figures throughout.
music-streaming-1.motif: The programme card: every work renders as a typographic concert programme — composer, work, opus, then the recordings listed like a season's casts — a form so print-native it survives unchanged into the diary export.

ia.coreObject: The work, with its shelf of recordings; each recording carries conductor, orchestra, soloists, year, and runtime
ia.primaryLoop: The listener searches by work, chooses among recordings or follows an editorial pick, plays it through their own Apple Music or Spotify, and returns to rate it and write a line in the listening diary, which slowly becomes their own annotated repertoire.

screens.title: Where does your music live?
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: connect the streaming account that will do the actual playing, stated without apology.
screens.hero: Two service cards on charcoal, with the division of labor spelled out beneath.
screens.data: Buttons: 'Connect Apple Music' · 'Connect Spotify'. Line: 'We hold no audio. We're the catalog and the programme; your subscription is the orchestra.' Connected state: 'Apple Music ✓ — 4 recordings of tonight's search already in your library.'

screens.title: Search by the thing itself
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: mid-search, demonstrating that the unit here is the work, not the album.
screens.hero: A large search field with results as programme cards, composer above work title.
screens.data: Query: 'eroica'. Result: 'Beethoven — Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, Op. 55 «Eroica» · 68 recordings, 1944–2024'. Below: 'Also matches: Strauss — Ein Heldenleben (frequently paired)'. Recent searches: 'Goldberg Variations', 'Mahler 5', 'Ravel string quartet'.

screens.title: Symphony No. 3 «Eroica»
screens.purpose: The work page: the full shelf of recordings, sortable the way collectors actually argue.
screens.hero: The programme card as header, then the recording list with conductor names set largest.
screens.data: 'Karajan · Berliner Philharmoniker · 1963 · 52:10'. 'Kleiber E. · Wiener Philharmoniker · 1955 · 49:47 (mono)'. 'Savall · Le Concert des Nations · 2020 · 44:58, period instruments'. Sorts: year, runtime, 'most in diaries'. Filter chips: stereo only, period instruments, live.

screens.title: The 1963 Karajan
screens.purpose: Recording detail: full cast and provenance, with one brass play button that hands off to the user's service.
screens.hero: A single programme card for this recording, cast listed like a playbill, play button at the bottom.

screens.purpose: The side-by-side comparison, the feature the whole audience argues about at dinner.

screens.data: Runtime deltas per movement: I. 14:22 vs 12:40 (−1:42). A/B rail: 'Funeral March, bar 1' — tap left plays Karajan in Apple Music, tap right Savall. Note field mid-compare: 'Savall's timpani are cannon fire; Karajan mourns in marble.' Footer: 'Handoff takes ~2 s per switch — your service does the seeking.'

screens.title: Where to begin
screens.purpose: Editorial picks: a first recording for newcomers to a work, argued in two sentences, never a score.
screens.hero: One laureled programme card with a short signed editorial note.
screens.data: 'Starting the Eroica? — Kleiber E., 1955. The mono sound is a small price for the most inevitable-feeling first movement on record. When it clicks, come back for Savall's shock therapy. — Ed.' Link: 'All 6 editor notes for this work'.

screens.title: Listening diary
screens.purpose: The personal record: dated entries binding a recording, a rating, and a line of the listener's own.
screens.hero: A reverse-chronological ledger of small programme cards, each gilded with the user's rating.

screens.title: Rate the evening

screens.hero: The just-played recording's card with five brass stars and a single text line.
screens.data: Detected via the connected service: 'You just finished: Eroica — Savall, 2020.' Stars set: ★★★★★. Line typed: 'Convinced. The horns at the finale are a different piece of music.' Buttons: 'File to diary' · 'Compare with my Karajan entry'.

screens.hero: A print-styled preview: the diary set as an actual season programme booklet.

screens.purpose: Service connections, catalog preferences, and data control, brief as a colophon.
screens.hero: A short grouped list on charcoal with the connected-service card on top.
screens.data: Service: Apple Music ✓ · switch to Spotify. Catalog: 'Prefer stereo remasters when both exist — on', 'Show mono recordings — on'. Diary: export, 'Back up to iCloud — on'. Editorial: 'New notes for works in my diary — monthly email'. Subscription: annual · renews Mar 2027 · Manage · Restore purchase.

notes-pkm-5.territory: It's exam week, three hundred handwritten pages deep, and the student needs the one lecture where the professor derived that formula — the old dread of knowing you wrote it down and not knowing where. The interface answers like a well-ordered workshop: paper-white, graphite-quiet, tools hung exactly where the hand expects them, and a search that treats your own handwriting as first-class text. Craftsman's calm instead of feature-fair noise.

palette.note: The accent is non-photo drafting blue, the pencil that doesn't reproduce: it marks search hits, selection handles, and OCR states, sitting under the user's own ink the way a draftsman's grid sits under a drawing.

notes-pkm-5.typography: Founders Grotesk for the sparse UI chrome, deliberately recessive, because the display face of this app is the user's own handwriting; page numbers and search counts in a monospaced Founders Mono like tool markings.
notes-pkm-5.motif: The blue underlay: found words in your handwriting lift on a soft drafting-blue highlight that follows the actual ink strokes, not a rectangle, making 'your handwriting is real text here' visible in one glance.

ia.coreObject: A handwritten page inside a notebook, carrying an invisible on-device text layer
ia.primaryLoop: Write by stylus through every lecture or meeting, then at crunch time ask the search bar for any word ever written; the recognizer keeps indexing quietly on-device so the answer arrives in a second, even from a first-year notebook.

screens.title: Touch pen to paper
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: prove the writing feel immediately, before any account or promise.
screens.hero: A live blank page with the user's first strokes already rendering, latency counter shown once like a spec plate.
screens.data: Prompt in light gray handwriting-style guide: 'Write anything — your name, a formula.' After a stroke: '9 ms pen-to-ink · pressure and tilt active'. One button: 'Keep this page' (it becomes page 1 of their first notebook).

screens.title: Read this once
screens.purpose: Second onboarding step: the on-device recognition promise, the single trust decision this audience makes.
screens.hero: A diagram of one page with the text layer peeling off it, arrows pointing only to the device chip, never a cloud.
screens.data: 'Your handwriting becomes searchable text on this iPad. Nothing is sent anywhere — recognition runs on-device (Apple Vision), works in airplane mode.' Sub-line: 'First index of an imported notebook: about 1 min per 100 pages, in the background.' Button: 'Understood, let's write'.

screens.title: Organic Chemistry II · page 47
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: a real lecture in progress, tools present but shy.
screens.hero: A full-bleed handwritten page with diagrams, a slim tool rail (pen, highlighter, eraser, lasso) docked left.
screens.data: Page content: reaction mechanism sketch, margin note 'ASK: why does Markovnikov fail here??'. Status line, tiny: 'p. 47 · indexed ✓'. Notebook header: 'Org Chem II — Spring '26 · 112 pages'. No toolbar ribbons, no template tray.

screens.title: Find · across every notebook
screens.purpose: The hero mechanic: one word from any year, found in a second, across all notebooks at once.
screens.hero: A search field over result cards, each a thumbnail of the actual handwritten page with the blue underlay glowing beneath the found strokes.
screens.data: Query: 'markovnikov'. Results: 'Org Chem II, p. 47 — today', 'Org Chem I, p. 89 — Oct 14, 2024', 'Exam prep, p. 3 — Dec 2024'. Count: '7 matches in 3 notebooks · 0.4 s'. Filter chips: this notebook, this year, PDFs too.

screens.title: Jump to the ink
screens.purpose: Search landing: the found page opens with the exact strokes lifted, the payoff moment of the whole product.
screens.hero: Page 89 of a 2024 notebook, the word 'Markovnikov' underlaid in drafting blue mid-paragraph of dense handwriting.
screens.data: Toast: 'Found on p. 89 — written Oct 14, 2024'. Next/previous match arrows in the corner: '2 of 7'. The user's two-year-old marginal doodle is untouched around the highlight.

screens.title: PDF · annotate the reading
screens.purpose: The second pillar: PDF annotation that stays put across reopen and export.
screens.hero: A journal-article PDF with handwritten margin notes and a highlighter pass, position-lock note visible on first use.
screens.data: File: 'Clayden_Ch12_alkenes.pdf · 24 pp'. Margin ink: 'this contradicts lecture!! see p. 47'. First-use note: 'Annotations anchor to the page geometry — they will not drift on reopen or export.' Search demo hint: 'Your margin notes are searchable too.'

screens.title: Export with the text layer
screens.purpose: The third pillar: a notebook leaves the app as a PDF whose handwriting is still findable outside it.
screens.hero: An export sheet showing the same page twice: visual (ink) and its invisible text layer revealed as an overlay toggle.
screens.data: 'Org Chem II → PDF · 112 pages · 38 MB · text layer: on.' Toggle preview shows selectable text ghosted over the ink. Line: 'Cmd-F works on this file in any PDF reader — your notes stay searchable after graduation.' Targets: Files, AirDrop, print.

screens.title: The shelf
screens.purpose: The notebook library: years of subjects at a glance, index health visible per notebook.
screens.hero: A grid of notebook spines with handwritten-cover thumbnails, each carrying a tiny index status mark.
screens.data: 'Org Chem II — 112 pp ✓', 'Linear Algebra — 203 pp ✓', 'Imported: GoodNotes backup — 641 pp · indexing, 74%', 'Lab journal — 58 pp ✓'. Sort: recent, subject, year. Total footer: '1,014 pages · all searchable'.

screens.title: Indexing an old life
screens.purpose: The background-work state after a big import: honest progress, nothing blocked.
screens.hero: The imported notebook open and fully writable, with a slim drafting-blue progress hairline under the header.
screens.data: 'GoodNotes backup: 474 / 641 pages indexed · ~2 min left · you can write and search the finished part now.' Note: 'Indexing pauses on low battery and resumes itself.' Never shown: a modal wait screen.

screens.title: A fresh notebook smell
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state on the shelf, for the minute before the first notebook exists.
screens.hero: One empty shelf slot rendered as a debossed rectangle with a pencil-sketch plus sign.
screens.data: 'No notebooks yet. Start blank, or bring your past: import from GoodNotes, Notability, or any PDF — old pages become searchable too.' Buttons: 'New notebook' · 'Import'. Sub-line: 'Your onboarding page is saved as «First page».'

screens.purpose: The paywall: a one-time purchase framed exactly like the tools this audience already bought once.
screens.hero: A single price plate, machined and plain, with the three promises engraved as the feature list.
screens.data: '$12.99, once. 1) Stylus writing with no page or notebook limits. 2) Handwriting search across everything, on-device. 3) PDF annotation and text-layer export.' Below: 'Free to try: 1 notebook, 30 pages, full search — no time limit.' Optional line, separate and quiet: 'Subject template packs (medicine, law, engineering) — $2.99 each, never required.' Footer, equal weight: 'Restore purchase' · 'No subscription, ever, is the product'.

screens.title: Tools
screens.purpose: Settings kept to a craftsman's minimum: pen defaults, recognition languages, backup, and data exit.
screens.hero: A short grouped list with the pen-feel block on top.
screens.data: Pen: default 0.4 mm graphite, palm rejection strict, left-handed mode off. Recognition: English + German, 'runs on-device only' (not a toggle, a statement). Backup: iCloud, encrypted, last: 11:20 today. Data: 'Export all notebooks (PDF w/ text layer, ZIP)'. About: version 1.2 · 'What the $12.99 bought you' changelog.

nutrition-calories-8.territory: The person opening this app has been hurt by numbers: they arrive braced for a verdict, half-expecting the app to grade their plate. The interface answers with the warmth of a linen-covered journal that never talks back, so 'energy and honest numbers' becomes honest absence of numbers, and the energy is the quiet relief of being unobserved. Every surface says: nothing here is keeping score.

palette.note: Warm linen ground with soft clay used only for gentle invitations, never for warnings, badges, or anything that could read as a grade on food.

nutrition-calories-8.typography: Tiempos Text for meal notes and pattern prose so the diary reads like a book rather than a dashboard, Untitled Sans for labels and controls; not a single numeral appears near a photo of food.
nutrition-calories-8.motif: Twin hunger dots on a soft arc bracketing every meal photo, before on the left and after on the right, positioned along a word-scale from 'ravenous' to 'past full' so the story of a meal is told without one number.

ia.coreObject: The meal entry: one photo plus three optional word-based fields (hunger before, fullness after, context)
ia.primaryLoop: Photograph the meal in five seconds, optionally slide two word-dots and pick a context, then once a month read the patterns page like a letter about yourself.

screens.title: What this diary will never do
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: state the anti-features as the product promise before asking for anything.
screens.hero: A plain white card with four short lines, each beginning with 'No' in clay: No calories. No scores. No comments on your plate. No streaks to break.
screens.data: Single line beneath the card: 'Built with the mindful eating protocol used in eating disorder recovery.' One button: 'That's what I need'.

screens.title: Check-ins, if you want them
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: opt into gentle prompts and set their tone and times, with off as an equal first-class choice.
screens.hero: Three sample prompt cards shown in the app's own voice so the user knows exactly what they are agreeing to.
screens.data: Sample prompts: 'How are you doing today, have you eaten?' at 1:30 PM, 'Evening. No need to log, just checking in.' at 8:00 PM. Toggle default: off. Button: 'Start my diary'.

screens.title: Today
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: today's meals as a quiet photo column, nothing counted, nothing missing flagged.
screens.hero: Three photo cards with generous white borders, each bracketed by the twin hunger dots on their arc.
screens.data: 8:10 AM, oatmeal with banana, before: 'quite hungry', after: 'comfortable', context: 'at the table, alone'. 1:45 PM, leftover pasta, before: 'a little hungry', after: 'comfortable', context: 'at my desk'. 7:30 PM, photo just added, fields still blank and left blank without any prompt to fill them.

screens.title: New entry
screens.purpose: The five-second log: camera first, three optional fields after, all skippable without friction or nag.
screens.hero: The just-taken photo filling the upper half, three collapsed optional rows beneath.
screens.data: Hunger before word-scale: ravenous, quite hungry, a little hungry, not hungry. Fullness after: still hungry, comfortable, full, past full. Context chips: at the table, on the go, at my desk, with others, alone. Save button active from the moment the photo exists.

screens.title: A check-in arrives
screens.purpose: Show the gentle prompt mechanic at its moment: a question, not a demand, with no red badge and no guilt copy.
screens.hero: A soft clay-bordered card sliding over Today, dismissible with one swipe that costs nothing.
screens.data: 'How are you doing today, have you eaten?' Buttons: 'I ate, want to add it', 'I ate, no photo today', 'Not yet'. Choosing 'I ate, no photo today' quietly adds an unphotographed entry dot to the day.

screens.title: Patterns, March
