password-manager-3.territory: The user has lived the lockout: new phone, dead codes, an evening pleading with support for accounts that were theirs. They arrive mistrustful of clouds and promises. The interface answers with bank-vault dignity — warm paper, engraved type, no chrome — and treats the worst day as the design brief: every screen quietly proves the recovery kit exists, is current, and works without the old phone.

palette.note: Paper and iron-gall ink do the work; sealing-wax red appears only on the recovery kit and its check-in, so the one thing that saves you is always the reddest thing in the room.

password-manager-3.typography: Source Serif 4 for headings and prose (bookish, unhurried authority), IBM Plex Mono with wide tracking for the six-digit codes and the recovery key — letterpress-even, readable across a desk.
password-manager-3.motif: The kit seal — the recovery kit is drawn as a folded paper document with a wax seal that sits unbroken while your kit is verified and visibly cracks when the six-month check-in goes overdue.

ia.coreObject: the code (a TOTP secret with a paper-and-file backup)
ia.primaryLoop: Open, read the 30-second code, done; twice a year the app asks you to lay eyes on the key sheet so the worst day stays a two-minute errand.

screens.title: Built for the day you lose this phone

screens.hero: The folded kit document with its wax seal, drawn like a certificate.

screens.title: Your first code

period-cycle-2.territory: She is 49, exhausted by a body that stopped following its own rules, and tired of apps that talk to her like a teenager trying to conceive. The interface answers with adult body literacy: the composure of a well-kept medical file that happens to be hers, private, unpanicked, and useful at the doctor's desk. Nothing pink, nothing cute, nothing predicted.

palette.note: Cool grey-lilac ground with a muted aubergine reserved for the user's own logged facts; the palette never uses red for symptoms because a hot flash is data, not an alarm.

period-cycle-2.typography: Freight Text Pro for report prose and section heads to carry clinical-adult gravity, Söhne for logging controls and timestamps; symptom intensity is set in words and small caps, never in emoji.
period-cycle-2.motif: The strata timeline: each day renders as thin horizontal sediment layers, one band per symptom type (sleep, flashes, mood, triggers), so months of erratic data read like a geological core sample you can hand to a doctor.

ia.coreObject: The symptom event: a timestamped hot flash, sleep note, mood, or trigger with intensity and duration
ia.primaryLoop: Log a hot flash in one tap as it happens, glance at the day's strata each evening, and every few months compile the layers into a report the gynecologist can actually read.

screens.title: Your history, as it actually is
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: accept any surgical and medical history without forcing a menopause-stage label.
screens.hero: A plain checklist titled 'Anything here apply to you?' with 'none of these' and 'prefer not to say' as equal options.
screens.data: Options: hysterectomy, oophorectomy (one or both), endometrial ablation, hormone therapy currently, none of these, prefer not to say. Footer: 'We will never ask you to pick a menopause stage. Your data will describe it better than a label.'

screens.title: What do you want to track?
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: choose symptom bands and seed the first custom triggers.
screens.hero: Symptom band chips arranged as the strata they will become, with a free-text field for custom triggers pinned at the bottom.
screens.data: Preselected bands: hot flashes, night sweats, sleep, mood, brain fog, palpitations. Trigger field with examples already typed by others: coffee, red wine, work stress. Button: 'Start the journal'.

screens.title: Today
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: the day's strata so far, with the one-tap flash button always within thumb reach.
screens.hero: Today's core sample: five thin stacked bands with events marked, and a large round 'Hot flash' button fixed bottom right.
screens.data: Tuesday, March 24. Sleep band: 5h 10m, woke 3:12 AM night sweat. Flash band: 2 events, 9:40 AM moderate 4 min, 2:15 PM strong 6 min. Trigger band: coffee 8:30 AM. Mood: 'flat, functional'. Quick-add row: night sweat, palpitation, brain fog, custom.

screens.title: Hot flash, one tap
screens.purpose: The one-tap log at its moment: the tap records the timestamp instantly, details are optional afterthoughts.
screens.hero: A confirmation sheet that has already saved, with intensity and duration as adjustable words rather than required inputs.
screens.data: 'Logged at 2:15 PM.' Intensity: mild, moderate, strong (strong selected). Duration: about 6 minutes, adjusted by dragging. 'What came just before?' chips from her own triggers: coffee, wine, stress, rushing, nothing I noticed. Close by swiping down, everything already saved.

screens.title: 3:12 AM
screens.purpose: Night mode state: logging a night sweat half-awake must not burn her retinas or her patience.
screens.hero: A near-black single-purpose screen with two oversized buttons and nothing else, entered automatically between 11 PM and 6 AM.
screens.data: Dark surface #1C1720, text #D8CFE0. Buttons: 'Night sweat' and 'Awake, can't sleep'. Tapping either logs the timestamp and dims back to black in two seconds. Small line: 'Details can wait until morning.'

screens.title: Calendar without predictions
screens.purpose: Show erratic cycles as recorded fact: gaps of any length are normal here, and no algorithm guesses the next period.
screens.hero: A month grid where bleeding days are simply marked in aubergine, with cycle lengths listed as plain history underneath.
screens.data: Recorded cycles: 24 days, 51 days, 33 days, 89 days, current gap 41 days and counting. No projected dates anywhere. Caption: 'Nothing here is predicted. This is what happened.'

screens.title: Your triggers
screens.purpose: Manage the custom trigger vocabulary that makes correlations personal instead of generic.
screens.hero: An editable list of her own words with per-trigger event counts, plus an add field with no preset ceiling.
screens.data: coffee, 41 logged. red wine, 12 logged. spicy food, 7 logged. presentation days, 5 logged (added by her, exists in no preset list). 'Add a trigger' field. Swipe to rename or merge triggers.

screens.title: What lines up
screens.purpose: Correlations across the strata: careful, counted observations that earn the doctor report its credibility.
screens.hero: Paired strata excerpts showing the trigger band above the flash band for the matched days.
screens.data: 'Red wine evenings were followed by night sweats within 6 hours on 9 of 12 occasions.' 'Nights under 5.5 hours of sleep were followed by brain fog logs the next day 14 of 19 times.' Footer: 'Counted from your 214 logged events. Correlation, not diagnosis.'

screens.title: Build the doctor report
screens.purpose: Choose the range and contents of the report that turns memory into data at the appointment.
screens.hero: A date-range selector over a shrunken core-sample preview of the whole period being exported.
screens.data: Range: October 1 to March 24 (176 days). Included: hot flash frequency and intensity by week, sleep summary, cycle record, top 3 trigger correlations, medication and history notes. Toggle each section. Button: 'Generate PDF'.

screens.title: Report preview
screens.purpose: The PDF as the gynecologist will see it: dense, sober, skimmable in the four minutes an appointment allows.
screens.hero: Page 1 of the PDF: the strata timeline compressed to one horizontal band per month with a summary table beneath.
screens.data: Header: 'Symptom journal, Oct 1 2025 to Mar 24 2026, prepared by the patient.' Table: hot flashes 3.1 per day average, peak week Feb 9 at 5.4 per day; night sweats 11 per month; cycles recorded: 24, 51, 33, 89 days. History: endometrial ablation 2021. Footnote: 'All entries timestamped at the moment of logging.'

screens.title: Worth a subscription
screens.purpose: Paywall matched to an adult audience: plain math against what she already spends, no urgency theatrics.
screens.hero: One sober sentence above two price cards: 'Flo charges $35 a month for a perimenopause tier. This journal is $4.58.'
screens.data: Yearly $54.99 (that is $4.58 a month), highlighted only by order. Monthly $9.99. Both include: unlimited logging, night mode, correlations, unlimited doctor reports. Free forever: logging and calendar. Footer links, equal size: 'Restore purchase', 'Keep the free journal', 'Privacy policy'.

screens.title: Day one
screens.purpose: Empty state: make the first log effortless and set the expectation that sparse data is still good data.

screens.data: 'Your first layer starts with one tap. Even three logs a week builds a report your doctor can use.' Buttons: 'Log something now', 'Set up night mode'.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Privacy, night window, data export, and history editing, treated as the adult controls they are.

screens.data: Privacy: data stays on this device, app lock with Face ID on, 'no analytics on health data' stated in plain text. Night mode window: 11:00 PM to 6:00 AM. Medical history: edit any time. Export: full CSV. Delete: 'Erase journal permanently', two-step.

personal-finance-10.territory: This person has kept a register for twenty years and has been burned by apps that redesign, resell, or guess. They arrive wanting to verify, not to be motivated. The interface answers with the daylight calm of a well-ruled paper ledger: quiet competence, numbers that are right to the cent, and the unspoken promise that nothing here will move next year.

palette.note: Ledger-paper white with fountain-pen blue for actions and entered amounts; a single reserved green check marks reconciled transactions and appears nowhere else in the app.

personal-finance-10.typography: IBM Plex Sans for labels and IBM Plex Mono for every amount, date, and balance, so columns of figures align to the cent the way a ruled ledger page does.
personal-finance-10.motif: The running balance column: a right-aligned monospaced balance beside every row on every list, ruled off by a hairline, extending unbroken from the first transaction into any future date you scroll to.

ia.coreObject: The transaction: a hand-entered debit, credit, transfer, or scheduled entry that moves the running balance
ia.primaryLoop: Enter the day's transactions by hand in seconds each, watch the running balance stay exact, and check the calendar to see the precise balance on any day ahead.

pet-care-5.territory: The owner is crouched on the kitchen floor at 6 a.m. cleaning up vomit, worried and half-awake; two weeks later they are in an exam room being asked 'when did it start?'. The interface answers with warm, unfussy competence: logging faster than opening Notes, no alarming conclusions, and by appointment day the worry has quietly become dates and frequencies a vet can actually use.

palette.note: Warm oat keeps 6 a.m. logging gentle on the eyes; scrub-green is reserved for done states and the vet summary, episode types get muted clay and ochre chips, and alarm red is never used.

pet-care-5.typography: Recoleta for headings (a soft bookish serif, like a well-kept pet journal), Inter for logs; numbers switch to strict tabular figures only inside the vet summary, because that page is for the clinic.
pet-care-5.motif: The knotted line — each condition's timeline is a single soft cord running left to right with a knot per episode, thickening where episodes cluster, so the trend is visible before you read a number.

ia.coreObject: the episode (one observed event with time, media, and note)
ia.primaryLoop: Something happens, you log it in ten seconds; the app ties it into the condition's cord and has the summary ready when an appointment nears.

screens.hero: A round pet photo above a short form, nothing clinical yet.

photo-editing-9.territory: A freelancer is mid-composite on a client poster, on a train, with a deadline tonight: their livelihood is stacked in that layer rail. The interface answers with the precision-darkroom calm of neutral chrome that recedes around the artwork, and with structural steadiness: tools sit where they sat yesterday, and nothing you paid for can vanish. Dark, because the canvas is the only thing allowed to glow.

palette.note: Neutral graphite chrome that stays colorless so the artwork owns all saturation, with a single safelight amber marking the active layer, the active tool, and nothing decorative.

photo-editing-9.typography: Archivo for tool labels and panels with Archivo Expanded for project titles, set small and dense like darkroom instrument markings, with tabular numerals for every pixel value and percentage.
photo-editing-9.motif: The layer rail with physical edge tabs: every layer is a tab protruding from the right screen edge like sheets in a lightbox stack, and the amber safelight strip runs the full height of whichever tab is active.

ia.coreObject: The project: a layered composition with an open, PSD-compatible file structure
ia.primaryLoop: Open a work-format template or a client file, stack and mask layers on the phone between other jobs, and export a deliverable or a PSD the desktop can open without loss.

plant-care-4.territory: The propagator checks a jar of water every morning with a collector's patience and a seller's stake: weeks of waiting where the only news is a millimeter of white root. The interface answers with botanical calm rendered as a paper field guide, herbarium labels and unhurried timelines that honor slow progress instead of demanding daily engagement. Nothing here rushes a root.

palette.note: Cream field-notebook paper with chlorophyll green appearing only where life does, on root progress, stage advances, and due water changes, never as generic UI chrome.

plant-care-4.typography: Newsreader italic for species binomials and stage names to echo herbarium labels, Work Sans for dates, methods, and controls; Latin names are always set in italic as a botanist would.
plant-care-4.motif: The root line: a fine green thread descending from every cutting's photo, growing longer and branching as stages pass, so a shelf of cuttings reads at a glance as a row of roots reaching down through paper.

ia.coreObject: The cutting card: species, method, date taken, conditions, and its staged timeline from snip to established plant
ia.primaryLoop: Check the shelf each morning, do the due water changes and moss checks the app surfaces, add the weekly root photo, and every few weeks enjoy converting a rooted cutting into a plant card.

screens.title: What are you rooting?
screens.purpose: Single-step onboarding: log the first cutting immediately, because the user already has one in hand.
screens.hero: A blank herbarium label card with four fields and a photo slot, styled like a field-guide specimen entry.
screens.data: Species: 'Monstera adansonii var. laniata' (free text with autocomplete). Method: water, sphagnum moss, soil, air layer. Date taken: today. Conditions: bright indirect, 72°F, humidity dome off. Button: 'Start the record'.

screens.title: The shelf
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: every active cutting as a specimen card, root lines descending, due tasks quietly flagged.
screens.hero: A two-column shelf of cutting cards, each with its photo, italic binomial, method chip, and its root line grown to current stage.
screens.data: 'Monstera adansonii', water, day 19, first roots, water change due today. 'Philodendron gloriosum', moss, day 34, roots 4 cm, moss check in 2 days. 'Begonia maculata', water, day 8, callus stage. 'Hoya carnosa', soil, day 51, ready for hardening off, flagged in green. Counter: '4 active cuttings'.

screens.title: New cutting
screens.purpose: The full cutting card mechanic: species, method, date, and conditions captured in under a minute.
screens.hero: The herbarium label form with the method choice as four small botanical diagrams (jar, moss ball, pot, wrapped stem).
screens.data: Species: 'Philodendron micans'. Method: sphagnum moss. Date taken: March 24. Light: east window. Temperature: 70°F. Notes: 'node had aerial root already'. On save: 'Moss schedule set: check moisture every 4 days, first root check March 31.'

screens.title: Cutting timeline
screens.purpose: One cutting's full story: stages, photos, and interventions on a single vertical record.
screens.hero: The root line as the timeline's spine, with weekly root photos attached at their dates and stage markers as labeled nodes.
screens.data: 'Monstera adansonii', water. Mar 5: cut, photo. Mar 9: water changed. Mar 12: callus formed. Mar 17: first roots, 0.5 cm, photo. Mar 21: water changed. Mar 24: roots 2 cm, photo due today. Next node, ghosted: 'move to soil, typically day 25 to 40 for this genus'.

screens.title: Water change due
screens.purpose: The method-specific reminder at its moment: a small honest task, logged with one tap, schedule adjusts to your habit.
screens.hero: A due card with the cutting's photo and a single green action, plus the schedule rationale in small print.
screens.data: 'Monstera adansonii, water change, every 4 days, last changed March 21.' Buttons: 'Changed it', 'Snooze to tomorrow'. Small print: 'Water-rooted cuttings need fresh water every 3 to 7 days to keep oxygen up. Your rhythm: every 4 days.' Also due: 'Philodendron gloriosum, vent the humidity dome, 10 minutes'.

screens.title: Time for soil
screens.purpose: The stage-advance moment: roots long enough, the app proposes the move and sets up the transition care.
screens.hero: A side-by-side of the March 17 and March 24 root photos with the measured growth called out on the root line.
screens.data: 'Roots reached about 4 cm. For water-rooted Monstera, 3 to 5 cm is the usual moving range.' Buttons: 'Moved to soil today', 'Give it another week'. On confirm: 'Transition care: keep soil lightly moist for 14 days, expect one droopy week, that is normal.'

screens.title: Seedling mode
screens.purpose: The parallel mode for seed-starters: denser watering cadence until roots establish, then a stepped shift to adult rhythm.
screens.hero: A tray card holding multiple seedling cells under one record, with a cadence bar showing the current phase.
screens.data: 'Sinningia speciosa, sown March 2, 9 of 12 germinated.' Phase: establishment, mist daily. Cadence bar: mist daily (now, day 22) → water every 2 days (after true leaves) → adult rhythm every 5 to 7 days. Next check-in: 'thin the weakest 3 seedlings this week'.

screens.title: Graduation
screens.purpose: The one-tap conversion of a rooted cutting into a permanent collection card, full history carried over.
screens.hero: The cutting card visibly re-labeling itself: the root line curls into a small rosette badge on the new plant card.
screens.data: 'Hoya carnosa, day 58: hardened off.' Button: 'Add to collection'. Result card: 'Hoya carnosa, propagated by you, water method, 58 days from cutting to plant, full timeline and 9 photos attached.' Note: 'Sellers: the record makes a nice provenance card for buyers.'

screens.title: Genus playbooks
screens.purpose: The paid method templates at their moment of value: genus-specific stages and timings loaded into a new cutting.
screens.hero: A field-guide page for one genus with its method comparison table and expected timing bands.
screens.data: 'Hoya: water 3 to 8 weeks, moss 2 to 6 weeks, higher success in moss above 65% humidity. Common stall: cutting stays green but rootless past week 8, re-cut the callus.' Playbooks shelf: Monstera, Philodendron, Hoya, Begonia, Syngonium. Badge: 'Included with Field Kit'.

screens.title: Field Kit
screens.purpose: The paywall, collector-honest: free covers 3 active cuttings forever, the upgrade is priced under one rooted rare cutting.
screens.hero: A paper price card with the root-line motif underlining the one-time option.
screens.data: Free: 3 active cuttings, all reminders, timelines, conversion. Field Kit one-time $7.99: unlimited active cuttings, seedling trays, photo compare. Field Kit annual $14.99 a year: everything plus genus playbooks, new genera added each season. Line: 'One sold rooted Hoya covers either.' Buttons: 'Buy once $7.99', 'Annual $14.99', 'Restore purchase'.

screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: an invitation written for someone who already propagates, not a tutorial.
screens.hero: An empty specimen card slot drawn in dotted field-guide linework with a jar illustration.
screens.data: 'Your first cutting goes here. Log it at the snip and the record starts clean: method, date, conditions, and every root photo after.' Button: 'Log a cutting'. Small line: 'Already have cuttings going? Backdate them, the schedule adjusts.'

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Reminder windows, units, and data ownership, kept as calm as the rest of the notebook.
screens.hero: A short grouped list on cream paper with the reminder window as the first control.
screens.data: Reminder window: mornings 8:00 to 10:00 AM. Units: °F, cm (mixed units allowed). Photo quality: high. Export: full records with photos as PDF or CSV. iCloud backup: on. Notifications: due tasks only, 'no engagement nudges, ever' stated in plain text.

pregnancy-tracker-5.territory: The person was fit before, feels like a stranger in her own body this week, and is quietly grieving the workouts she used to do. The interface answers with unhurried warmth and zero clinical edge: it never measures her against her old self, it meets today's energy exactly where it is. Everything breathes slowly; nothing counts down, flashes or pushes.

palette.note: Blush-cream ground with white session cards; terracotta is reserved for the current week's pebble and the single primary action, so warmth accumulates instead of shouting.

pregnancy-tracker-5.typography: Fraunces (soft optical sizes) for headings and week names, Nunito Sans for body and cues; headings sit large and low-contrast, like a well-designed prenatal book rather than a fitness app.
pregnancy-tracker-5.motif: The pebble string: forty hand-drawn rounded stones arcing across the top of every screen, one warming to terracotta per week, and after birth a second smaller string of twelve begins for the fourth trimester.

ia.coreObject: This week's session, tuned to trimester and today's energy
ia.primaryLoop: Each morning she answers one soft question about today's energy, gets a session sized to it, and returns because the program visibly moves with her body week by week.

screens.title: Onboarding · Where are you
screens.purpose: Anchor the whole product to her week with one gentle input.
screens.hero: The pebble string forming as she scrolls a due-date wheel
screens.data: Prompt: 'When is your baby due?' Set: 'November 12'. Response beneath: 'Week 22 — second trimester. Your program starts here, not at week one.' Alternate link: 'I've already given birth'.

screens.title: Onboarding · How you moved before
screens.purpose: Respect her history so sessions start at the right intensity, without promising her old body back.
screens.hero: Three plain choice cards, no body imagery
screens.data: Prompt: 'Before pregnancy, movement was…' Options: 'A big part of my life — I trained most days', 'Regular but casual', 'I'm starting fresh'. Selected: first. Note: 'We'll keep real work in your sessions. Some weeks will still ask for less, and that's the program working.'

screens.title: First morning (empty state)

screens.title: Today, mid-use

screens.hero: Today's session card with its length and focus, pebble 22 glowing
screens.data: Greeting: 'Wednesday · week 22'. Card: 'Mobility & breath — 18 min · hips, mid-back, diaphragm'. Below: 'This week your relaxin is loosening joints, so we hold stretches shorter.' Secondary: 'Wednesday check-in: how's your energy?'

screens.title: Energy check-in
screens.purpose: The adaptive mechanic earning its keep: a rough day reshapes the session without guilt.
screens.hero: A single horizontal slider between 'wrung out' and 'ready for more', large and slow
screens.data: Prompt: 'How is today, honestly?' Set near low end. Result card: 'Then let's do 9 minutes: floor-based breath and gentle hips. Skipping the rest costs you nothing — the program picks you up where you are on Friday.'

screens.title: Session player
screens.purpose: Mid-exercise clarity with breath as the metronome instead of a countdown clock.
screens.hero: A full-bleed illustrated pose with a slowly expanding and contracting halo synced to breath
screens.data: Exercise: 'Supported squat hold, 2 of 3'. Cue text: 'Exhale as you rise. Heels stay heavy.' Breath halo labeled 'in — 4 · out — 6'. Modification chip: 'Wrists sore? Fists or forearms.' Next up: 'Side-lying leg lift'.

screens.purpose: The block nobody else ships as a real program, taught with plain technique.
screens.hero: A two-track program card: 'Foundation' and 'Birth prep', weeks marked on each
screens.data: Foundation: 'Session 4 of 10 — finding a full release, 8 min'. Technique note: 'A strong pelvic floor also knows how to let go — today is about the letting go.' Birth prep (unlocks week 30): 'Breathing for stage one · positions that use gravity'.

screens.title: Fourth trimester
screens.purpose: Show the postpartum program as a first-class stage, not an epilogue.
screens.hero: The second, smaller pebble string of twelve beginning where the forty end

screens.purpose: Prove variety so she trusts she is not looping two flows for months.

screens.data: Filter: 'Second trimester'. Rows: 'Strength — 14 sessions', 'Mobility — 11', 'Breath & rest — 8', 'Pelvic floor — 10', 'Walk companions — 6'. Card sample: 'Strength: pull day with band, 22 min · new this week'.

screens.data: Headline: 'One program from week 6 to twelve weeks after birth.' Line: '₽599/month · your first week is fully open, no card needed to start it'. Included: 'Every stage, pelvic floor & birth prep, fourth trimester, energy-adapted sessions'. Links: 'Restore purchase' · 'What's free forever: weekly check-ins and walk companions'.

qr-scanner-7.territory: The volunteer at the door has a line of forty people, a phone that isn't theirs, and thirty seconds of training, while the organizer paces behind them praying the Wi-Fi doesn't matter. The interface answers with traffic-signal certainty: one camera, one verdict filling the whole screen, readable from a meter away in a dark doorway, no judgment calls left to the volunteer.

palette.note: The interface is a dark viewfinder frame so the three verdict floods, signal green, amber, and red, carry the entire meaning, and no other element ever uses those three colors.

qr-scanner-7.typography: Barlow Semi Condensed for verdicts and names at doorway sizes, IBM Plex Mono for counters and timestamps: condensed weight buys huge letters on small screens, mono makes every count auditable.
qr-scanner-7.motif: The verdict flood: on every scan the whole screen becomes the answer, edge-to-edge color with one word and one name, visible over a shoulder from across the door.

ia.coreObject: The guest list, loaded once, living whole inside every phone at the door
ia.primaryLoop: For each recurring meeting the organizer loads the list, volunteers open a link and scan, and the merged report of who came pulls the organizer back after every event.

recipes-meal-planning-1.territory: The person planning this week's meals does math before every bite, and one wrong recipe means a blood sugar spike at 2 AM. The interface answers with kitchen daylight where the arithmetic is already done: warm, appetizing food photography sitting on top of numbers that are exact, visible, and never hidden behind a tap. Appetite and safety on the same screen, neither apologizing for the other.

palette.note: Warm kitchen white with a calm teal meaning 'within your carb budget'; amber appears only when a meal approaches its cap, and the palette never uses red on food because dinner is not an emergency.

recipes-meal-planning-1.typography: Fraunces for recipe names to keep food warm and appetizing, Plus Jakarta Sans with tabular numerals for every gram count, so the carb math always reads as instrumentation, not decoration.
recipes-meal-planning-1.motif: The carb badge and budget bar pair: every recipe photo carries a bottom-left badge ('22 g carbs / serving') and every meal slot in the week carries a slim budget bar filling toward its cap, one visual grammar from library to plate.

ia.coreObject: The planned meal: a recipe with pre-calculated carbs, GI, and GL per serving, placed in a slot with a carb cap
ia.primaryLoop: Each Sunday build the week within per-meal carb caps, each day cook from the plan and shop from the auto list, and never hand-check a recipe against the endocrinologist's tables again.

screens.title: Your carb budget
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: set per-meal and daily caps once, in the same units the endocrinologist uses.
screens.hero: Three meal-slot cards each with its own gram cap stepper, summing live into a daily total at the bottom.
screens.data: Breakfast cap: 30 g. Lunch: 45 g. Dinner: 25 g. Snacks: 20 g. Daily total: 120 g. Note: 'Per-meal caps matter more than the daily total for insulin dosing. Change these anytime.' Button: 'Next'.

screens.title: What's off the table?
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: exclusions and household size so the 400-recipe library filters to what this kitchen actually cooks.
screens.hero: Ingredient exclusion chips over a household servings stepper.
screens.data: Exclusions: shellfish, cilantro selected from: pork, shellfish, nuts, dairy, gluten, cilantro. Cooking for: 2 people. Weeknight time limit: 40 minutes. Result line: '317 of 400 recipes fit your kitchen.' Button: 'Build my first week'.

screens.title: This week
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: the planned week with every meal's budget bar visible, tonight's dinner one tap away.
screens.hero: A seven-day grid where each filled slot shows its dish, carb badge, and slim teal budget bar against the slot's cap.
screens.data: Tue dinner: 'Skillet chicken with cauliflower mash, 21 g / 25 g cap'. Wed lunch: 'Lentil soup with side salad, 38 g / 45 g'. Wed dinner: 'Zucchini lasagna, 24 g / 25 g', bar nearly full in amber. Thu breakfast: empty slot, ghost text '30 g available'. Week header: 'Planned: 19 of 21 meals'.

screens.title: Recipe: Zucchini lasagna
screens.purpose: The recipe detail where the numbers earn trust: carbs, GI, and GL per serving stated with their basis.
screens.hero: Full-bleed photo with the carb badge, then a numbers block set above the ingredients, not below.
screens.data: Per serving (1 of 6): carbs 24 g, fiber 6 g, glycemic index 28 (low), glycemic load 6.7. Basis line: 'Calculated from USDA entries for the exact quantities below.' Time: 55 min. Ingredients with grams: zucchini 700 g, ricotta 250 g, passata 300 g. Buttons: 'Plan it', 'Swap an ingredient'.

screens.title: Serving slider
screens.purpose: The instant recalculation mechanic: scale servings and watch every number move with it.
screens.hero: A horizontal serving slider under the numbers block, all gram values re-rendering live as it drags.
screens.data: Slider at 1 serving: 24 g carbs, GL 6.7. Dragged to 1.5 servings: 36 g carbs, GL 10.1, and a quiet amber note appears: 'At 1.5 servings this exceeds your 25 g dinner cap by 11 g.' Dragged back to 1: note dissolves. Ingredient quantities scale in place: zucchini 700 g → 1,050 g → 700 g.

screens.title: Swap the potato
screens.purpose: Built-in low-carb swaps at their moment: substitute inside a recipe and see the carb delta before committing.
screens.hero: A swap sheet listing alternatives for the selected ingredient, each with its per-serving carb delta as the primary label.
screens.data: In 'Beef stew': potato 320 g, contributes 18 g carbs per serving. Swaps: cauliflower florets, -14 g. turnip, -11 g. celeriac, -12 g. Choosing cauliflower updates the badge live: 31 g → 17 g per serving, GL 12.4 → 5.9, and adds a note to the method: 'add cauliflower in the last 20 minutes'.

screens.title: This one doesn't fit
screens.purpose: The conflict state: a chosen recipe would break the meal cap, and the app resolves it without shaming or blocking.
screens.hero: The over-cap slot with its budget bar overflowing in amber and three concrete ways out stacked beneath.
screens.data: 'Butternut risotto is 41 g per serving. Your dinner cap is 25 g.' Options: 'Swap the rice for cauliflower rice, brings it to 22 g', 'Move it to lunch, 45 g cap, fits with 4 g to spare', 'Plan a 0.6 serving portion, 25 g, smaller plate'. No option is preselected.

screens.data: '21 empty slots, every one already knows its carb cap.' Buttons: 'Fill the week for me, using your caps and exclusions' and 'Plan meal by meal'. Small line: 'Auto-filled weeks respect every cap. You can swap any meal after.'

resume-builder-6.territory: The person is applying to a role they actually want, oscillating between ambition and the fear of looking sloppy or losing an hour of writing to a flaky editor. The interface answers like a fine stationer: composed, typographically exact, visibly saving every keystroke, so the applicant feels like someone who sends impeccable paper.

palette.note: An oxblood accent behaves like a wax seal, appearing only on the stitch that binds the packet and on the send action, while the documents themselves stay pure black on white.

resume-builder-6.typography: Lyon Text for document previews and headings, Graphik for the editing chrome: the reader's serif makes every preview feel already printed, the sans keeps the tooling invisible.
resume-builder-6.motif: The stitch: three document edges bound by a single oxblood thread, appearing wherever resume, letter, and references travel as one packet.

ia.coreObject: The packet, resume plus cover letter plus references in one matching design, tied to one opening
ia.primaryLoop: For each real opening, spin up a packet from the resume already on file, tune the letter, and send one impeccable set, then track which packet went where.

ride-hailing-5.territory: It is 11:40 PM, a regular is in the back seat, and this driver is not a gig worker but a one-person business whose reputation rides on a clean invoice. The interface answers with the dashboard confidence of professional night equipment: map-first, glanceable at arm's length, every dollar accounted to the penny. Dark because the cabin is dark, legible because the car is moving.

palette.note: Deep night-cabin navy with taxi-heritage yellow carrying only live money and active states, so the running fare is always the brightest thing on a dark dashboard.

ride-hailing-5.typography: Barlow, a typeface literally drawn from transport signage, in SemiBold for fares and Regular for detail, with tabular numerals sized so the running meter is readable from a phone mount at arm's length.
ride-hailing-5.motif: The fare tape: a receipt-tape strip that runs through the whole product, ticking line by line on the live meter, printing as the invoice, and stacking into monthly statements, one continuous paper trail from wheel to reimbursement.

ia.coreObject: The trip: a GPS-tracked ride metered against the driver's own rate card, ending in an invoice
ia.primaryLoop: Start the meter at pickup, end the trip and send the to-the-penny invoice before the client reaches the lobby, and watch regulars rebook through your own page.

screens.title: Your rate card
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: the driver sets their own rates, the numbers that define the whole business.
screens.hero: The rate card as a fare-tape form, each line item appearing on the tape as it is set.
screens.data: Base fare $6.00. Per mile $2.75. Per minute $0.55. Minimum fare $18.00. Night surcharge 10 PM to 5 AM: +20%. Holiday surcharge: +25%. Airport flat option: BWI $72.00. Footer: 'Rates are yours. Updates never touch them.' Button: 'Next'.

screens.title: Your business identity
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: the details that make invoices reimbursable at the client's employer.

screens.data: Business name: 'Delgado Private Car'. Driver: Marcus Delgado. Phone, email. EIN (optional): filled. Payment note: 'Card via Square, cash, Zelle'. Preview stamp: 'This header appears on every invoice and statement.' Button: 'Open the meter'.

screens.purpose: The main screen mid-trip at night: live fare, route trail, and the tape ticking, all readable from the mount.
screens.hero: The running fare in huge yellow tabular Barlow over a dimmed live map with the GPS trail drawn solid behind the car.
screens.data: Fare so far: $34.85. Elapsed: 22:41. Distance: 9.3 mi. Line items ticking on the tape: base $6.00, 9.3 mi x $2.75 = $25.58, 22.7 min x $0.55 = $12.49, night +20% pending at stop. Client chip: 'K. Osei, pickup 11:18 PM, Penn Station'. One button: 'End trip'.

screens.title: Call comes in, meter holds

screens.data: Live activity: 'Meter running: $41.20, 11.6 mi, 28:03'. Incoming call: 'Dispatch, mobile'. Status line inside the app afterward: 'GPS track continuous: 0 gaps in the last 28 minutes, screen was off 6 of them.' Small print: 'The meter runs in the background by design. Calls, navigation, and lock screen never pause it.'

screens.title: Trip complete

Fields present: payment method (Visa via Square), driver signature, business address. Send: text, email, or PDF. Line: 'Totals are computed once, from the meter. The invoice cannot drift from the charge.'

screens.purpose: Settings for a business owner: identity, tax exports, payment rails, and data ownership.

GPS: precision high, battery note stated honestly ('about 6% per hour metered'). Backup: iCloud on. Support: 'a human answers within a day'.

run-tracking-1.territory: The person is a beginner who has quit before, standing at the door half-expecting the plan to humiliate them again. The interface answers with open-air lightness and a coach's short sentences: it visibly listens after every run, so the dominant feeling shifts from bracing to being accompanied.

palette.note: A high-visibility trail-marker orange is spent only on the next step and live effort, everything else stays morning-sky quiet so mid-run glances land in one saccade.

run-tracking-1.typography: Archivo in its expanded cuts for splits and countdown numerals, with Inter for coach lines: wide confident figures you can read at arm swing, plain speech everywhere else.
run-tracking-1.motif: The inserted rung: the whole plan is drawn as a vertical ladder, and when the plan rewrites itself a new rung physically slides in between two existing ones.

ia.coreObject: The next workout, a single rung the plan re-earns after every run
ia.primaryLoop: Run the session, rate the effort with one tap, watch the ladder rearrange itself and the countdown to 5K update, come back tomorrow because the next rung fits.

screens.title: Where you actually are
screens.purpose: Two-step onboarding: a starting question and permissions, no fitness interrogation.
screens.hero: One question card with three plain answers
screens.data: Step 1: Right now, how long can you run without stopping? Choices: Under 1 minute, 1 to 5 minutes, 5 minutes or more. Step 2: heart rate source, Apple Watch connected, and location for pace. Footer: The plan corrects itself after every run anyway.

screens.title: Today's rung
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-plan: exactly one workout, sized by the last one.
screens.hero: A single large rung card with the ladder faintly visible behind it
screens.data: Week 4, run 2 of 3. Session: 5 rounds of run 3:00, walk 1:30, total 27 min with warmup. Coach line: Last run's effort was a 5, so this holds the same step before we lengthen. Button: Start. Below: 9 workouts to 5K.

screens.title: Mid-run
screens.purpose: Split-second legibility while moving, interval state above all else.
screens.hero: A full-width interval band, orange while running, sky while walking, with a giant countdown
screens.data: Run · 1:47 left in this interval · round 3 of 5. Secondary row: 14:22 elapsed, heart rate 168, pace 7:41 per km. Haptic cue note: two taps at interval change. Hold to pause.

screens.title: One question after
screens.purpose: The single input the whole algorithm runs on, asked once, then silence.
screens.hero: A 1-to-10 effort dial big enough for a shaking thumb
screens.data: How hard was that? Dial set to 8. Anchor labels only at 1, could talk the whole time, and 10, could not have done one more round. Footer: heart rate last 5 min: avg 172, that's 88% of your max 195. Button: Done.

screens.title: The plan rewrites itself
screens.purpose: The signature moment: the ladder animates and a new rung slides in, with one line of why.
screens.hero: The vertical ladder with a 6-minute rung visibly sliding between the 5 and the 8
screens.data: Inserted: run 6:00 continuous, Thursday. Why line: An 8 out of 10 with a high late heart rate means the jump from 5 to 8 minutes was too big, so a 6 goes in between. Countdown adjusts: 10 workouts to 5K, was 9.

screens.title: Recovery goes first
screens.purpose: The heart-rate rule earning its keep: above 85% in the final five minutes triggers a recovery session.
screens.hero: A soft sky-colored rung marked Recovery ahead of the next orange step
screens.data: Your heart rate held above 85% of max for the last 5 minutes. Tomorrow: 20 easy minutes, walk-run as you like, effort target 3. Coach line: This is the plan working, not the plan slipping.

screens.title: Missed day, moved rung
screens.purpose: Skipped-day state: the workout relocates itself and nothing is lost or scolded.
screens.hero: Yesterday's rung shown sliding down one slot on the ladder
screens.data: Tuesday's run moved to Wednesday. Streak note absent by design. Line: Your 9 workouts to 5K is unchanged, the ladder just shifted a day. Button: See this week.

screens.title: Fast track unlocked
screens.purpose: Three easy runs in a row let the plan skip intermediate rungs, momentum rewarded honestly.
screens.hero: Two grayed rungs folding out of the ladder as it shortens
screens.data: Efforts of 3, 4, 3 across your last three runs. Skipping: run 8:00 and run 10:00, next up run 12:00 continuous. Countdown drops: 6 workouts to 5K, was 8. Option: Keep the original steps instead.

screens.title: Countdown to the line
screens.purpose: Progress view centered on the one number a beginner actually holds onto.
screens.hero: A huge expanded-Archivo numeral over the full ladder from couch to 5K
screens.data: 7 workouts to 5K. Ladder below with 17 rungs done in solid orange, 7 hollow. History row: longest continuous run so far 8:00, up from 0:45 in week 1. No pace charts, no VO2 anything.

screens.title: The part that listens
screens.purpose: Paywall after the second rewrite, when the user has felt the adaptation twice, framed against the rigid template they came from.
screens.hero: Side-by-side ladders: a fixed 9-week template versus their own ladder with its inserted rungs highlighted
screens.data: The base 9-week plan stays free forever. The plan that rewrites itself after every run, plus your full history: $8 a month, or $39 once, yours for good. Comparison line: Runna is $15.99 a month and never inserts a step. Buttons: Start adaptive, Pay once $39, Restore purchase, Keep the free plan.

screens.title: Before the first run
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: no data, one honest promise, one button.
screens.hero: An empty ladder with only the first rung solid
screens.data: Nothing to show yet, everything here gets built from your runs. First rung: walk 5:00, run 1:00, repeat 4 times, about 24 min. Line: After it, one question, and the plan takes over. Button: Start run 1.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The few controls a beginner needs, worded like a coach, not a lab.
screens.hero: Short grouped list
screens.data: Max heart rate: 195, edit. Audio cues: at interval changes only. Units: kilometers. Run days: Tue, Thu, Sat. Plan: adaptive, active. Purchases: Restore purchase. Export runs as GPX.

scanner-pdf-6.territory: Hour two of digitizing a grandmother's diary, arm cramping, page 214 of 400. The fear is not effort, it is loss: one crash eating the afternoon. The interface answers like a good bench tool: zero decoration, a counter that only climbs, and constant quiet proof that every page is already safe on the device.

palette.note: Archival green, the color of library binding cloth, marks exactly two things: a page confirmed written to disk and a completed project; everything else is ink on paper.

scanner-pdf-6.typography: Public Sans throughout with tabular numerals, because the page counter is the emotional center of the product; nothing decorative survives, and labels read like tool engravings.
scanner-pdf-6.motif: The fold line: a hairline running down the center of every frame where the spread splits into verso and recto, echoed in miniature by the gap map's grid of tiny page squares.

shopping-ecommerce-7.territory: The hunter knows exactly which coat, which colorway, which size, and has been circling it across four outlets for months: the feeling is patient, connoisseur desire, sharpened by the outlets' little markup games. The interface answers with editorial-retail restraint: gallery white space where the coveted object is presented like a plate in a lookbook, and the data underneath is cold, exact, and on the hunter's side.

palette.note: Gallery white with near-black type, and a single vermilion that fires only at the moment of the catch: the alert, the target hit, the size still in stock; the rest of the interface stays as quiet as a lookbook.

shopping-ecommerce-7.typography: Canela for item names and editorial headings to carry the fashion-plate desire, Neue Haas Grotesk for sizes, prices, and history data, so lust and evidence never share a typeface.
shopping-ecommerce-7.motif: The hunt line: a thin price-history thread drawn under every item like a hem stitch, with the hunter's target price marked as a vermilion notch, so one glance shows how close the quarry is to the trap.

ia.coreObject: The hunted item: one specific past-season piece in one size, with its target price and cross-outlet price history
ia.primaryLoop: Save a piece and a size, check the watchlist's hunt lines the way you check weather, and act within the hour when the vermilion alert says your size hit your price.

sleep-tracking-8.territory: It is 11:40 pm, the mind is loud, and the last thing this person can handle is another storefront of choices. The interface answers with the depth of night itself: three soft questions, one glowing path, and a screen that dims as they descend toward sleep. Nothing asks for a decision after the third answer.

palette.note: No pure white exists anywhere; everything glows like moonlight, and the whole screen dims stepwise as the program plays, brightness returning only with the morning check-in.

sleep-tracking-8.typography: Tiempos Text carries the three questions in a soft near-white serif while Söhne Mono keeps the small numerals (block timers, minutes-to-sleep) quiet and exact; type stays large and low-contrast so nothing jolts the eyes at 1 a.m.
sleep-tracking-8.motif: The descent: every evening is one vertical path of three softly glowing stops (breath, body, sound) that dim one by one as you pass them, the screen literally darkening toward sleep.

ia.primaryLoop: Answer three questions at bedtime, run the program, tap once in the morning; the two-week review quietly tunes what tomorrow's program leans on.

sobriety-2.territory: The person opens the app at the worst minute of their day, heart rate up, willpower thinning, needing something to hold for fifteen minutes. The interface answers with dawn-light steadiness: warm, unhurried, zero friction before the button, treating the user as someone strong who is riding a wave, not a patient being managed.

palette.note: Terracotta is warmth, not alarm: it colors the craving button and the rising arc, and it never flashes, pulses, or turns red no matter what the user logs.

sobriety-2.typography: Canela for the few sentences that matter, held or not, the pattern insights, with Untitled Sans for everything operational: gentle serif moments inside a plainspoken frame.
sobriety-2.motif: The dawn arc: a horizon line with a sun that climbs for exactly fifteen minutes, the app's clock, its progress bar, and its promise that peaks pass.

ia.coreObject: The urge entry, one tap plus two tags, which becomes cartography over weeks
ia.primaryLoop: Hit the button at the peak, ride the fifteen-minute arc with an activity, answer held or not, and return later to see which hours and situations pull hardest.

screens.hero: The craving button shown at full size with the arc behind it
screens.data: Step 1: When an urge hits, tap once. A 15-minute timer starts, because peaks pass in 15 to 20 minutes. No login, no streak required. Step 2: Add the button to your lock screen and home screen. Skippable. Nothing else asked, not even the substance.

screens.hero: A tag grid floating over the arc, which has already started climbing

screens.data: 8:52 remaining. Chosen activity: walk to the corner and back. Alternatives one swipe away: 4-7-8 breathing, glass of water, text Sam. Single line at the horizon: The peak is usually behind you before the sun is up. No exit penalty, leaving keeps the entry.

screens.data: 15 minutes done. Did it hold? Buttons: It held · It didn't this time. If it didn't: one optional tag, no lecture, line reads: You logged it at the peak, that's the hard part. Entry saved either way, 24th ride recorded.

step-counter-5.territory: The person just finished forty minutes on a treadmill, or crossed a parking lot with a walker, and knows from experience that their phone will pretend none of it happened. The interface answers with light, friendly matter-of-factness: every kind of real movement gets counted, labeled and believed, with no interrogation and no asterisk of shame. It should feel like a scorekeeper who is finally on your side.

palette.note: Airy sky-tinted ground with white cards; coral marks today's total and primary actions, while each step source keeps its own steady secondary hue (watch teal, phone gray, treadmill plum, hand-added always hatched) so the bars read at a glance.

step-counter-5.typography: Rubik throughout with tabular numerals for totals; round terminals keep the numbers friendly, and source labels sit in small caps-free 13pt so honesty never looks like fine print.
step-counter-5.motif: Source stripes: every daily total is a single stacked bar striped by where the steps came from, and hand-added stripes are always diagonally hatched, in today's ring, in history, everywhere.

ia.coreObject: A day of movement assembled from labeled sources
ia.primaryLoop: The watch streams steps all day while the person adds the movement sensors miss (treadmill, catch-up, rowing), and they come back each evening to see the day made whole.

screens.title: Onboarding · Your main counter

screens.data: Prompt: 'Where do your steps really happen?' Options: 'Apple Watch (recommended primary)', 'Fitness band via Health', 'Phone only'. Selected: Apple Watch. Note: 'Phone steps fill gaps only when the watch is off — never double-counted.'

stock-investing-4.territory: The person owns four positions in a brokerage app they're mildly afraid to open, and every red number feels like an accusation written in a language they never learned. The interface answers with the warmth of good financial print: newsprint paper, patient serif prose, and the standing promise that any number on screen will explain itself in plain words on a single tap. Precision without the terminal's cold stare.

palette.note: Salmon-tinted newsprint ground with lighter paper cards; the deep bottle green marks everything tappable-for-explanation and every lesson action, while gains/losses stay in muted ink-red and ink-green that never flash or animate.

stock-investing-4.typography: Tiempos Text for lessons and explanations, IBM Plex Mono for every figure; prose reads like a patient financial column and numbers sit apart in mono so 'words explain, figures inform' is visible in the type itself.
stock-investing-4.motif: The dotted underline: every number and term that can explain itself wears a newsprint-dotted green underline, and the underline is the product's entire promise — nothing wears it without a plain-English answer behind it.

translator-1.territory: The person is mid-shift at a bedside, slightly rushed, carrying the fear of getting a dosage word wrong in front of a patient who is already anxious. The interface answers with clinical composure: two languages held in equal dignity, nothing decorative, every tap defensible to a charge nurse.

palette.note: A scrubs-teal accent marks only verified clinical terms and the speak button, so color itself certifies that a word came from the checked vocabulary.

translator-1.typography: Source Serif 4 for patient-facing bedside text and Public Sans for the caregiver's controls: the serif reads warm and human when the screen turns toward the patient, the sans stays procedural on the working side.
translator-1.motif: The seam: a thin horizontal rule dividing the two languages on every screen, which rotates the top half 180 degrees when the phone is laid flat between caregiver and patient.

voice-recorder-5.territory: The person knows the sentence they need exists somewhere in years of recordings and feels the low dread of scrubbing through hours to find it. The interface answers with control-room composure: dark, unhurried, engineered, where a typed question lights up the exact seconds that matter across the whole archive.

palette.note: VU-meter amber is the color of a hit: it marks live recording level and found moments on timelines, and nothing else in the interface is ever amber.

voice-recorder-5.typography: IBM Plex Mono for timestamps, durations, and counters, IBM Plex Sans for titles and transcripts: the mono ties every piece of text back to a position on tape.
voice-recorder-5.motif: Lit ticks on the tape: every recording is a horizontal waveform strip, and search results appear as amber ticks glowing at their exact second, visible even at archive zoom.

ia.coreObject: The moment, a timestamped span inside a recording, reachable by question
ia.primaryLoop: Record or import as life happens, then return with questions, and every answered question makes the years-deep archive worth more.

wallpapers-widgets-7.territory: The person is in a season of waiting — the trip booked, the graduation date set — and they check the number the way you touch a ticket in your pocket. The interface answers with quiet ceremony: their own photo does all the talking, one truthful number sits on top of it, and the app never asks for more attention than a glance.

palette.note: The UI stays near-monochrome so the user's event photo is the only saturated thing on screen; boarding-pass amber marks milestones and the midnight tick, nothing else.

wallpapers-widgets-7.typography: Fraunces for the big day numeral (soft warm serif, tabular figures, never bolded), SF Pro Text for everything else; the numeral is the brand and it is set enormous.
wallpapers-widgets-7.motif: The anchored numeral — the day count always sits in the same lower-left anchor over a soft photo scrim, so every widget, card and screen reads as the same object at different sizes.

ia.coreObject: the event (a date with a photo)
ia.primaryLoop: Glance at the home-screen number each morning; open the app only when a milestone card arrives or a new wait begins.

wardrobe-outfit-8.territory: She has just paid for the answer she has wanted since her first color-analysis video, half thrilled, half braced to be told her closet is wrong. The interface answers like a trusted fashion editor: composed ivory pages, one confident verdict instead of a wall of palettes, and no judgment — every item gets a way forward: wear it, rescue it, or release it.

palette.note: The chrome stays ivory-and-ink like a magazine page so garment photos and the twelve season palettes supply all the color; plum is the editor's pen — verdicts and annotations, nothing else.

wardrobe-outfit-8.typography: Canela for verdicts and headlines (high-fashion serif with warmth), Söhne for labels and data; the season name is set enormous, like a cover line, because the answer is the product.
wardrobe-outfit-8.motif: The woven label — every verdict renders as a stitched garment care label (Yours / Neutral / Not yours) sewn onto the corner of each item photo, the same label that appears full-width under your season.

ia.coreObject: the verdict (your season, and each item's tag against it)
ia.primaryLoop: Snap new items and morning candidates against the palette; before any purchase, the pocket palette settles the shade in the fitting room.

water-hydration-1.territory: The user has ADHD or a condition and no reliable thirst signal, and they arrive vigilant — two trackers have already gone silent on them. The interface answers with clear, glassy calm and a visible heartbeat: proof on the lock screen that the system is alive, nudges that arrive like water lapping until answered, and total, earned silence once the day is won.

palette.note: Everything sits in pale poolside light; the only strong color is the water itself — the fill line — and red appears exactly once in the whole app, inside the diagnostic when iOS is confirmed to be suppressing you.

water-hydration-1.typography: SF Pro Rounded for the big tabular day total and buttons, Inter for body; soft round terminals keep a nudge that repeats every ten minutes feeling patient instead of nagging.
water-hydration-1.motif: The meniscus — every progress element is a waterline with a curved surface-tension edge that tilts subtly with device motion, from the lock-screen bar to the day ring.

ia.coreObject: the day's waterline
ia.primaryLoop: Log from the lock screen when nudged; nudge → log → next nudge recalculated from that sip runs itself until the goal closes the day in silence.

screens.title: Reminders that answer to your last sip
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: set the goal and state the difference — the timer starts from your log, not from the clock.
screens.hero: A horizontal timeline where a log at 2:40 PM visibly pushes the next nudge to 4:40 PM.
screens.data: Goal 2,000 ml · wake 7:30 · sleep 23:00; caption 'Drink at 2:40 and the next nudge comes at 4:40 — two hours from the sip, not from a grid.'

screens.title: Keep iOS convinced
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: permissions plus the honest explanation of why the Live Activity exists.
screens.hero: A rendered lock screen with the meniscus bar sitting under the clock.
screens.data: Toggle 'Allow notifications'; card 'iOS quietly drops reminders from apps it thinks you've abandoned. Our lock-screen bar with a log button counts as direct contact, so yours never vanish.' Button 'Add the lock-screen bar'.

screens.title: First sip starts the loop
screens.purpose: First-day empty state: a waterline at zero that asks for one action, not a tour.
screens.hero: An empty vessel outline the full height of the screen, meniscus resting at the bottom.
screens.data: 0 / 2,000 ml; three preset drops: 250 ml · 350 ml · 500 ml; footnote 'Your first log schedules your first reminder.'

screens.title: Today, 2:47 PM
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: where the day stands and exactly when the next nudge lands.
screens.hero: The meniscus at 57%, tilting faintly as the phone moves.
screens.data: 1,150 / 2,000 ml · last log 2:40 PM (350 ml) · 'Next nudge 4:40 PM — two hours after your last sip'; quick drops 250 / 350 / 500 ml.

screens.title: The lock-screen bar
screens.purpose: The anti-suppression heartbeat at its earning-its-keep moment: log without unlocking.
screens.hero: A Live Activity strip: meniscus bar, count, one round +250 ml button.
screens.data: '1,150 ml · next 4:40 PM' with [+250] button; caption 'Tapping here is direct interaction — iOS keeps delivering.'

screens.title: Until you answer
screens.purpose: Show the repeat-until-logged mechanic as a visible, finite plan rather than mystery nagging.
screens.hero: A vertical chain of three identical notifications with ten-minute gaps, the chain ending at a log.
screens.data: 4:40 PM 'Water.' → 4:50 PM 'Water.' → 5:00 PM 'Water.' → 5:03 PM logged 350 ml, chain stops; note 'Same two words every time. You stop reading it and keep hearing it.'

screens.title: Done means quiet
screens.purpose: The goal-met state: silence as the reward, stated explicitly.
screens.hero: The meniscus resting at the brim, surface completely still for the first time all day.
screens.data: 2,000 / 2,000 ml at 8:12 PM; line 'Done. Not another sound until 7:30 tomorrow.'; reminders toggle shown auto-set to off until morning.

screens.title: Why your reminders die
screens.purpose: The self-diagnostic: the app inspects what is suppressing notifications and names it.
screens.hero: A checklist of delivery facts, one item flagged in the app's only red.
screens.data: 'Focus "Work" allows us ✓' · 'Sleep schedule 23:00–7:30 respected ✓' · 'Delivered 39 of 41 nudges this week' · flagged: 'Scheduled Summary is holding our 4:40 PM nudge until 6:00 PM — tap to fix in iOS Settings'.

screens.title: From the wrist
screens.purpose: Apple Watch logging that syncs instantly, with honesty about why the phone bar still matters.
screens.hero: A watch face complication showing the meniscus ring at 57%.
screens.data: Watch log +250 ml at 4:41 PM appears on phone in the same second; footnote 'Watch replies alone don't count as contact for iOS — the lock-screen bar covers that.'

screens.purpose: History without shame: a missed day is just a shorter bar.
screens.hero: Seven meniscus columns of varying height, none colored as failure.
screens.data: Mon 2,100 · Tue 1,650 · Wed 2,000 · Thu 400 · Fri 2,050 · Sat 1,900 · Sun 1,150 so far; caption under Thursday: 'You just picked up Friday. That's the whole plan.'

screens.purpose: Paywall matched to a buyer who has been burned twice: one price, the whole loop, nothing rented.
screens.hero: A single glass card listing the three things that kept dying elsewhere.
screens.data: '$9.99 once: lock-screen bar · repeat-until-logged · Apple Watch.' Line 'Free version logs water and shows history, forever.' Comparison stated plainly: 'Waterllama lifetime is $16.99 — reviews say that's why people buy.' Link 'Restore purchase'.

screens.purpose: Tuning for real medical routines without burying the defaults.

weather-apps-4.territory: This app is installed for one moment: 1 a.m., a funnel on the ground, a family asleep. Every other day it must earn trust by staying quiet. The interface answers with civil-defense clarity: white paper, instrument typography, timestamps you could hold up in court, and a red that is banned everywhere except the moment that matters.

palette.note: Signal red is forbidden on every ordinary surface, so when the whole screen turns red at 1 a.m. it can only mean one thing; all other days the app is black ink on white paper.

weather-apps-4.typography: IBM Plex Sans for instructions and IBM Plex Mono for every issued/delivered timestamp, set like an instrument log the user is invited to audit.
weather-apps-4.motif: The polygon: the actual NWS warning polygon drawn as a heavy red outline against your address pin. Inside the line means wake up; outside the line means we stay silent.

ia.coreObject: The warning: an NWS polygon stamped with issued and delivered times
ia.primaryLoop: Set it once and sleep; the daily habit is a five-second glance at the quiet all-clear badge and the delivery-latency log that keeps re-earning trust.

weight-tracker-2.territory: The person did the hard thing already, lost 60 pounds over two years, and now lives with a quiet background fear that it's all temporary. The interface answers with steady, judgment-free stewardship: not a coach, a lighthouse keeper. Numbers are presented the way a good accountant presents them, calmly and in context, and the only drama the app permits itself is an early, quiet word when the trend starts to drift.

palette.note: Cool paper-gray ground with white chart cards; the slate teal fills the corridor band at 8% opacity everywhere, deepening to full strength only on the trend line, so 'inside the band' is the calmest place on every screen.

weight-tracker-2.typography: Söhne for interface text and Söhne Mono for every weight figure; monospaced weights line up down the column like a ledger, making change legible and drama impossible.
weight-tracker-2.motif: The corridor band: a soft teal horizontal band the trend line lives inside on every chart, from onboarding sketch to year view — the product's entire promise drawn as one shape.

ia.coreObject: A maintenance corridor with a trend line inside it
ia.primaryLoop: A morning weigh-in feeds the moving average, the person glances at where the trend sits inside the band, and they return because days-inside-the-corridor is a streak worth protecting.

screens.title: Onboarding · Draw your corridor
screens.purpose: Replace the goal-number ritual with setting a livable range.
screens.hero: A vertical scale with two draggable handles forming the band between them
screens.data: Prompt: 'Where does your weight get to live?' Set: '150 – 156 lb'. Guidance line: 'Most people hold well in a 5–7 lb band around where they've been stable.' Current context field: 'Today I'm around: 152.5 lb'.

screens.title: Onboarding · Where you came from
screens.purpose: Honor the descent that came before so history has its full shape from day one.
screens.hero: A faded downhill line ending at the freshly drawn corridor band
screens.data: Prompt: 'How much did you lose to get here?' Entry: '61 lb since March 2024'. Import: 'Bring past weigh-ins from Apple Health (842 entries found)'. Note: 'Your descent stays in the picture. This app's job is what comes after it.'

screens.title: First week (empty state)
screens.purpose: The corridor exists but the trend doesn't yet; make the wait purposeful, not blank.
screens.hero: The empty band with two lonely dots and a dotted placeholder trend
screens.data: Band: 150–156. Dots: 'Jul 5 — 152.5', 'Jul 6 — 153.1'. Message: 'Your trend appears after 5 weigh-ins. Single days bounce — the moving average is what we watch, and it can't be spooked by one dinner.' Button: 'Set my weigh-in reminder'.

screens.title: Corridor, mid-use
screens.purpose: The daily glance seven months in: trend comfortably inside, streak alive.
screens.hero: The 90-day band chart with the trend line riding the lower-middle of the corridor
screens.data: Trend today: '152.8 lb — inside, 3.2 lb below the upper edge'. This morning: '153.4 (single days bounce; trend moved +0.05)'. Streak: '214 days inside the corridor'. Last weigh-in chip: 'Today 7:04 AM'.

screens.title: Drift signal
screens.purpose: The flagship mechanic at its earning moment: the calm early word, while it's still ounces.

workout-fitness-7.territory: Twelve minutes between calls, already in sneakers, zero patience for browsing. The person arrives with momentum and the interface answers with heat and arithmetic: bold type, one draining bar, and a clock that keeps its word to the second. The energy is a coach clapping once, not a brand shouting.

palette.note: Heat is spent on time alone: the bar, the countdown numerals and the word Done are the only orange things on screen, so the clock is always the loudest voice in the room.

workout-fitness-7.typography: Druk Wide for the minute count you asked for and Space Grotesk with tabular figures for everything counting down; the number 12 is the biggest object in the interface.
workout-fitness-7.motif: The honest bar: one uninterrupted horizontal bar equal to the minutes you asked for, warmup and cooldown drawn inside it, draining left to right and hitting zero at the promised second.

ai-writing-1.territory: He has read his own email four times and still hears his native language underneath the English, two minutes before sending it to a VP. The interface answers like a trusted senior editor at the next desk: a quiet typographic studio where his text stays his, every mark is small and precise, and each one comes with a one-line reason he can keep. The feeling on exit is not 'fixed' but 'slightly better at this than yesterday'.

palette.note: Warm gallery white with near-black text; the editor's-pencil red appears only as underlines and margin marks, so density of red literally shows how much was learned.

ai-writing-1.typography: Lyon Text for the user's prose, Suisse Int'l for interface chrome and margin notes: his email reads like set type on the page while the editor's voice stays in small, businesslike sans.
ai-writing-1.motif: The margin note: every correction is a fine red underline in the text tied by a hairline to a one-line explanation in the right margin, like a copyedited galley proof.

ia.coreObject: The pass: one piece of real writing plus the set of explained corrections made to it
ia.primaryLoop: Paste or type an email, run one pass, read the margin notes, send; he returns because every pass feeds the mistake log and his recurring habits visibly shrink.

ai-writing-3.territory: The novelist is twenty chapters deep at midnight, half in the story and half in fear that the book has started contradicting itself. The interface answers as a quiet study: the manuscript owns the center of the room in book type on ivory paper, and the machinery of memory works in the margin like a careful assistant who never speaks over the prose. Assistance should feel like a librarian sliding the right index card across the desk.

palette.note: Oxblood lives only in the margin, on bible references and continuity flags, while the manuscript itself stays pure ink on ivory so the writing is never decorated, only accompanied.

ai-writing-3.typography: Lyon Text sets the manuscript at a true book measure and Graphik handles the chrome and bible cards, so the writing always feels like the finished book and the tooling feels like the desk around it.
ai-writing-3.motif: The continuity thread: a hairline running down the manuscript margin, tying names in the prose to their bible cards, and visibly snagging into a small knot wherever a draft contradicts an established fact.

ia.coreObject: the chapter, written against the story bible
ia.primaryLoop: Outline a scene, let the co-writer continue in the author's own voice, untangle any snagged threads, and end each session with the bible one page richer.

baby-tracking-1.territory: It is 3:40 am, one parent is holding a bottle in the dark and the other is asleep with their phone on the pillow, and the only question that matters is 'does the other phone already know'. The interface answers with a whisper: dim warm surfaces, one-thumb logging, and a visible confirmation that the entry landed on the partner's phone, so nobody has to speak, text, or remember anything at dawn.

palette.note: A plum-charcoal night room lit by one warm apricot glow; brightness is capped so nothing on screen can wake a sleeping baby, and synced entries settle from apricot to cream as confirmation.

baby-tracking-1.typography: Nunito throughout, its rounded terminals doing the softness, with elapsed times in big 34pt semibold so '1h 48m ago' reads through half-open eyes.
baby-tracking-1.motif: The sync ripple: every entry that arrives from the partner's phone lands with a single slow concentric ripple, and every entry you make shows a small traveling dot from your phone icon to theirs, so synchronization is something you can literally watch happen.

ia.coreObject: The event (feed, sleep, diaper) with an event timestamp and the caregiver who logged it, merged across phones
ia.primaryLoop: Log each feed, sleep, and diaper in two taps at any hour, and glance at the status board to see what the other parent already handled.

baby-tracking-4.territory: Two babies, one adult, four hands short: the parent of twins lives in permanent parallel, feeding one while the other stirs, and every app makes them choose a profile first. The interface answers by refusing to make them choose: both children are always on screen, side by side, each in their own color, and acting on both is one gesture. It feels like finally having a second pair of eyes.

palette.note: Warm oat background with each baby owning a permanent pastel — Theo mint #2E9C8E, June lilac #A47BC4 — used consistently on timers, dots, and charts so color alone answers 'which baby' before any label is read.

baby-tracking-4.typography: Baloo 2 for names and numbers, plump and unhurried, with Inter for labels, so the two columns feel like matching cribs rather than a spreadsheet.
baby-tracking-4.motif: Twin lanes: two parallel vertical columns that never collapse into one, joined at moments of shared action by a soft horizontal bridge that lights up on long-press when an event logs to both babies at once.

ia.coreObject: The paired event: a feed, sleep, or diaper belonging to one baby or bridged across both, each stamped with its baby's color
ia.primaryLoop: Glance at both columns, tap to log for one twin or long-press to log for both, and check the drift chart to nudge two schedules back together.

blood-pressure-log-1.territory: The person is a 62-year-old doing homework their cardiologist assigned, slightly anxious about the numbers and more anxious about showing up to the appointment looking disorganized. The interface answers with the composure of a well-run clinic: big type, generous contrast, nothing blinking, every number already arranged the way a doctor reads it. It feels less like an app and more like a document that fills itself in.

palette.note: Near-black ink on warm paper white, with one clinical blue reserved for the current target and actions; readings above target are marked with the same ink weight plus a thin blue underline, never with alarming red.

blood-pressure-log-1.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for all text at 18pt minimum, with readings set in 40pt tabular figures, so the personality is simply legibility taken seriously enough to feel like care.
blood-pressure-log-1.motif: The visit sheet: a single ruled A4-proportioned page that every screen is visibly a fragment of, with thin horizontal rules and a printed-form header, so the user always feels the finished printout assembling underneath their daily entries.

ia.coreObject: The reading (systolic/diastolic/pulse, auto-tagged morning or evening), rolling up into the one-page visit report
ia.primaryLoop: Measure with the cuff twice a day, type three numbers in under fifteen seconds, and watch the visit-sheet countdown tick toward the appointment date.

calendars-tasks-3.territory: The person setting this up has been burned: a missed pill, a stove left on, a mother who swipes notifications away without reading. The moment of use is anxious dependence on a machine that has failed them before. The interface answers with daylight and certainty: enormous type, one thing per screen, and the audible presence of someone they love, so trust is rebuilt sound by sound.

palette.note: Warm daylight white with deep cobalt for actions; escalation is shown by the cobalt ripple rings warming toward amber as levels rise, so urgency is visible even with sound off.

calendars-tasks-3.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything, set two sizes larger than convention with 1.5 line height, because the target user may be 74 and the whole personality is 'built to be read'.
calendars-tasks-3.motif: The ripple: every reminder is a cobalt dot that radiates concentric rings, one ring per escalation level, so the interface itself pictures a sound that will not stop until touched.

ia.coreObject: The reminder: a time, a recorded voice, an escalation ladder, and a required confirmation
ia.primaryLoop: Record it once in a familiar voice, live your day, and when it fires it grows until you press Done, which is the entire relationship.

calendars-tasks-9.territory: A former paper-planner devotee misses the Sunday ritual of pens, stickers, and washi tape, but has been burned by a digital planner that lost months of handwritten pages. The interface answers with a craft desk in daylight, a printed calendar that never lies underneath and a hand-made layer on top, plus the quiet institutional confidence of visible backups. Orderly, yes, but the order is the user's own handwriting.

palette.note: The printed calendar layer stays in gray ink; almost all color arrives from what the user adds, ink, stickers, and tape, so every page feels authored rather than themed.

calendars-tasks-9.typography: Adobe Caslon small caps for the printed month and day names (the voice of a well-made paper planner) with Karla for app chrome; the user's own handwriting is the true display face and the type stays out of its way.
calendars-tasks-9.motif: The two-layer page: printed live events beneath, handwriting and tape above, with a light-table toggle that peels the layers apart so you can always see the calendar telling the truth underneath.

flashcards-1.territory: A medical student three weeks from an exam has months of labor compressed into one deck and a low-grade dread of losing it, because they have either lost one before or watched a classmate lose theirs. The interface answers like an archive with a reading room: the studying is tactile and fast, and underneath every card sits visible, timestamped proof that the work is safe and recoverable. Confidence here is not a slogan, it is a receipt.

palette.note: Cool archival paper with academic oxblood used only for study actions and the restore verb; sync receipts render in quiet gray monospace so safety reads as infrastructure, not decoration.

flashcards-1.typography: Source Serif 4 on card faces for textbook gravity, Inter for the interface, and IBM Plex Mono for every timestamp and sync receipt, because the ledger is the personality.
flashcards-1.motif: The version spine: beneath the active deck, the edges of its past snapshots peek out like sheets in a carbon-copy stack, each edge carrying a monospace timestamp tab, so history is physically present under today's work.

ia.coreObject: The deck, carried by an append-only edit ledger where every change has a timestamp and a device tag
ia.primaryLoop: Run the day's review reps, see the one-line receipt that every edit reached the cloud, and keep building the deck knowing any version of the last 90 days is two taps away.
