focus-productivity-6.territory: It is 8:52 in a classroom of 24 kids, or minute forty of a bedtime negotiation: the adult is stretched thin and the child cannot read a clock. The interface answers with instant legibility from across a room, one shape that IS the time, so calm that the timer never becomes more interesting than the task. Clarity here means a poster, not an app.

palette.note: The persimmon accent lives almost entirely inside the disk itself; all chrome stays chalk-neutral so nothing on screen competes with the time.

focus-productivity-6.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for every label (a typeface literally built for legibility, honest in a classroom), kept small and quiet because the disk is the typography and digits are hidden by default.
focus-productivity-6.motif: The whole-circle disk: any duration you pick fills the entire circle, so half the time always looks like exactly half the circle, no fractions, no clock math.

ia.coreObject: A timed moment: a single visual timer or one step inside a routine chain
ia.primaryLoop: Tap a duration or a chain, the disk fills full and shrinks while the child watches from anywhere in the room; mornings, transitions, and bedtimes repeat daily, so the timer does too.

invoice-maker-7.territory: A tradesperson between job sites, hands full, sun on the windshield, zero patience for admin. The interface answers with jobsite clarity: gloves-on tap targets, glance-legible numbers, and the quiet competence of a tool that already filed the trip to the right client before the truck door closed. It should feel like a well-organized van, not an accounting office.

palette.note: Safety orange means money, deductions earned and billable lines, while everything else stays in grayscale so the screen reads instantly in truck-cab sunlight.

invoice-maker-7.typography: IBM Plex Sans at heavy weights for glance-reading from a cupholder, with IBM Plex Mono for miles and dollars so every column lines up like a printed invoice.
invoice-maker-7.motif: The geofence stamp: every saved job site is a bold ring on a quiet map, and each visit punches the ring like a hole struck on a job card.

ia.coreObject: the trip, filed to a client
ia.primaryLoop: Drive the day as usual while arrivals at saved sites file themselves, then a ten-second evening swipe pass turns the day's driving into deductions and invoice lines.

journaling-mood-2.territory: The person opens the app in a fragile or flattened moment, sometimes at 2 am mid-episode, and the last thing they need is cheerfulness or friction. The interface answers with the privacy of a good paper ledger: cream, ink, quiet serif labels whose meaning never drifts. It feels permanent and exact, like a notebook a psychiatrist would trust.

palette.note: Ink on cream everywhere; the fountain-pen blue appears only as the pen itself, marking today's dots and the single primary action, never as decoration.

journaling-mood-2.typography: Tiempos Text for scale labels and headings, Söhne for numbers and interface chrome; the serif gives every level-word the fixed, printed authority of a form the doctor has seen a hundred times.
journaling-mood-2.motif: The ruled ledger line: each of the four scales is one horizontal rule with labeled stops, and today's state is a single ink dot pressed onto it, so a month reads as four steady lines of dots.

ia.coreObject: The daily entry: four labeled scale dots plus sleep hours and medications, exactly one per day
ia.primaryLoop: A 90-second evening check-in placing four dots and confirming meds; people come back because an unbroken ledger is what makes the next psychiatrist appointment actually work.

journaling-mood-4.territory: She opens it in the early morning or the last quiet minutes of the evening, carrying real weights: a father's biopsy, a daughter's move, a friend's marriage. The interface answers like a well-bound paper journal from a church bookstore: cream pages, ink, scripture set with reverence, and room for an answer to arrive months later. It never performs spirituality back at her; it keeps the record of a faith being practiced.

palette.note: Cream paper and warm ink with a single deep violet used like a ribbon and for the word 'Answered'; color never celebrates, it marks.

journaling-mood-4.typography: Adobe Caslon Pro for scripture and headings, Freight Text Pro for her own writing: a book voice, not an app voice, with verses set with true small caps and hanging quotes.
journaling-mood-4.motif: The ribbon: a thin violet satin bookmark hangs from the top edge of every screen, marking today's page, and moves when an old request is finally marked answered.

ia.coreObject: The request: a prayer with a date, the people it is for, and space for how it was answered
ia.primaryLoop: Morning verse and a look at open requests, three lines of gratitude in the evening; she returns because requests she planted months ago keep resolving, and the journal is where that becomes visible.

meal-prep-grocery-1.territory: It is Sunday afternoon and the user is trying to turn five recipe tabs into one trip to the store without buying a third bag of flour. The interface answers with the calm of a well-run kitchen: crisp lists, visible arithmetic, and the small satisfaction of watching two ingredient lines fold into one. Fresh and practical, never foodie-glossy.

palette.note: Market-fresh white with produce-green accents; green marks additions and merges, while 'have it at home' items fade to a soft strikethrough gray instead of disappearing, so the subtraction stays visible and trusted.

meal-prep-grocery-1.typography: Cabinet Grotesk for headings and day labels, Inter for list rows and quantities; friendly weight up top, utterly legible arithmetic below, like a good grocery receipt.
meal-prep-grocery-1.motif: The roll-up bracket: whenever ingredients merge, a thin green bracket visibly gathers the source recipe lines into the single combined line, keeping the math inspectable at a glance.

ia.coreObject: The week (a meal plan whose byproduct is one clean shopping list)
ia.primaryLoop: Pick recipes for the week, tap what's already at home, and walk the store with one deduplicated list; the growing recipe library and the shared plan with a partner are what bring both adults back every Sunday.

meditation-mindfulness-2.territory: Heart at 140, hands unsteady, a decision budget of about five seconds: the person cannot choose, read, or navigate. The interface answers with dusk-dark emptiness and exactly one thing happening, a slow amber horizon that breathes so they do not have to think about breathing. Everything else in the product exists to be configured earlier, in a calm hour, so the crisis screen can be almost nothing.

palette.note: Color barely moves: the warm amber horizon brightens on the inhale and settles on the exhale, and nothing else on screen changes at all.

meditation-mindfulness-2.typography: Söhne in exactly two sizes; during a protocol the type nearly disappears, one short line at a time, set large and low-contrast so it guides without demanding to be read.
meditation-mindfulness-2.motif: The dawn horizon: a soft amber band low on the screen that rises with every inhale and sinks with every exhale, the whole interface reduced to one slow tide.

ia.coreObject: A protocol: a pre-configured rescue scenario with a chosen voice, pace, and duration

notes-pkm-1.territory: Sunday evening, tea beside the iPad, the small ritual of setting up the week that Hobonichi people guard like a sacrament. The interface answers as a well-bound notebook would: it opens flat, stays quiet, and offers beautiful blank structure without ever selling another sheet of paper. The pleasure is in the tool disappearing under the pen.

palette.note: Warm cream paper under near-black ink, with Hobonichi vermillion appearing only as the printed grid accents and the current-day marker, exactly like red ink on a Japanese planner.

notes-pkm-1.typography: Tiempos Text for printed template labels and dates, set small and letterspaced like fine planner printing; the user's own handwriting is the real display face.
notes-pkm-1.motif: The stitched gutter: every spread has a true center seam with visible thread stitches, and pages turn around it with paper physics, so the app always reads as a bound book, never a canvas.

ia.coreObject: The notebook: a bound file of spreads (weekly, monthly, habit, budget) living as a document in iCloud
ia.primaryLoop: Open to this week's spread each morning, write plans and cross off yesterday in ink, and roll what is unfinished forward with one gesture on Sunday.

nutrition-calories-2.territory: The person logging is mid-flare or bracing for one, tired of being told it is stress, and quietly collecting evidence for a doctor who gets eleven minutes with them. The interface answers with clinical freshness: bright, unembarrassed, quick enough to use from a bathroom, and honest enough to say 'not enough data yet' out loud. It treats the gut like a system under study, not a failing.

palette.note: Clean white with a cool teal reserved for statistically confident findings; unconfirmed patterns stay grey so color itself encodes evidence.

nutrition-calories-2.typography: Söhne for interface text and Söhne Mono for timestamps and confidence figures, giving lab-report neutrality with warmth in the generous sizes.
nutrition-calories-2.motif: The delay arc: a thin arc that leaps across the day timeline from a food dot to a symptom dot, its span labeled 6h, 12h, or 24h, the app's entire thesis drawn as one line.

ia.coreObject: The day timeline: a single vertical strand holding food dots and symptom dots in true time
ia.primaryLoop: Two taps after eating, two taps when a symptom hits, then each Sunday the app surfaces which arcs kept repeating and the doctor report writes itself.

password-manager-1.territory: The user has finally decided to leave a password manager that holds 300 accounts hostage, and they are quietly afraid of losing even one. The interface answers with the dignity of a notary's office: warm paper, ledger rules, and numbers that reconcile in front of you. Nothing playful, nothing neon, just proof at every step that everything came across.

palette.note: Warm archival paper with deep-ink text; the bottle-green accent appears only where a count balances or an action is safe, and unparsed items use ink underlines, never alarm red, because loss here is information, not panic.

password-manager-1.typography: Source Serif 4 for headings and counts, Inter for UI labels and table cells; the serif carries certificate-grade gravity while tabular Inter keeps every reconciliation column honest.
password-manager-1.motif: The double-entry rule: every stage shows an 'in' figure and an 'out' figure joined by a hairline ledger rule, so the migration reads like a balanced book from start to finish.

ia.coreObject: The migration (one source file becoming one verified target file)
ia.primaryLoop: Drop an export file, watch fields map and counts reconcile, fix the stragglers, and walk away with a target file plus a report proving nothing was lost; most users come once, do the job, and leave satisfied, which is the point.

period-cycle-3.territory: She arrives wary, having just moved a decade of intimate medical history out of an app she no longer trusts, and she is checking whether this one deserves it. The interface answers like an archivist handing over the keys: calm, literate, adult, showing her the full record and the exit door in the same breath. Nothing pleads, nothing decorates, everything states.

palette.note: Warm archival paper with plum-black ink; the single garnet accent marks only what is hers to act on (export, backup, today), never decoration.

period-cycle-3.typography: Signifier for headings and cycle-day numerals, Söhne for interface text: the voice of a well-set medical memoir, literate and unhurried, with numerals large enough to read like facts rather than stats.
period-cycle-3.motif: The decade strip: her entire history rendered as one continuous horizontal band of cycle segments, like archival microfilm you can scroll back through ten years without a single chart.

ia.coreObject: The record: a single continuous, exportable cycle history that predates and outlives the app
ia.primaryLoop: She logs today in two taps, glances at where she is in the cycle, and returns because the record only stays complete if she keeps it, and the app keeps proving it stays hers.

personal-finance-1.territory: It is 9:40 pm on the sofa with a receipt still in the coat pocket: the user chose manual entry on principle, and the two seconds of typing the number is the whole ritual. The interface answers with the tactility of a well-made cash register in daylight, fast, physical, and done, so quiet competence comes from the act of entry rather than from dashboards.

personal-finance-1.typography: IBM Plex Mono for every number (tabular, columns always align, honest to the cent) with Inter for labels; the mono numerals carry the personality of a ledger, never a dashboard.
personal-finance-1.motif: The stamp: each saved entry lands with a small green ink-stamp mark, and every day you logged gets a stamped tick in the month ledger, so consistency is literally visible as ink.

personal-finance-2.territory: The person is standing at a register or hovering over a checkout button, mildly anxious, asking one question: can I afford this today. The interface answers with daylight certainty, one honest figure in warm morning light, math you can open like a receipt. No dashboard noise, no draining monthly balance, just today's number and the quiet satisfaction of watching yesterday's restraint slide into it.

palette.note: Color speaks only through the number itself, which shifts green, amber or red with the day's health, while the surrounding chrome never changes so the numeral is the entire weather report.

personal-finance-2.typography: GT America Mono carries every figure in tabular, unblinking digits while Untitled Sans handles the prose, so the daily number reads like an instrument and everything else stays out of its way.
personal-finance-2.motif: The rollover ribbon: at midnight, yesterday's unspent dollars slide under today's numeral as a thin folded paper strip docking into place, so discipline is literally seen adding itself to the day.

ia.coreObject: the day, a dated spendable number with its purchases attached
ia.primaryLoop: Check the number with morning coffee, log purchases in three taps as they happen, and come back at night to watch the leftover ribbon roll into tomorrow.

personal-finance-4.territory: It is the tenth of the month, the paycheck landed, and she is standing at her shelf of envelopes deciding what this month gets. The interface answers with daylight bookkeeping calm: flat paper pockets, exact figures, no charts and no commentary, the quiet competence of someone who has done this for years. Nothing here performs; a full envelope simply looks full.

palette.note: Cool daylight grey-green around white paper envelopes; the deep green ink is the fill inside envelopes and the confirm actions, so color literally is money allocated.

personal-finance-4.typography: Untitled Sans for interface text with all money set in Founders Grotesk Mono tabular figures: numbers align to the cent down every column, like a ledger kept by hand but never smudged.
personal-finance-4.motif: The paper pocket: every envelope is a flat white rectangle with a visible flap, filled from the bottom edge by a solid rising tint of green ink, so the whole month is readable as fill levels on a shelf.

ia.coreObject: The envelope: a named pocket with a balance, a limit, and its own refill schedule
ia.primaryLoop: She deducts a purchase from an envelope in two taps (often from the widget), glances at the shelf, and comes back because the shelf is the only true picture of what she can still spend.

personal-finance-8.territory: A self-employed person carries a low hum of tax dread all year: the shoebox of receipts, the miles nobody wrote down, the audit letter they imagine at 2 a.m. The interface answers with archival calm, everything filed the moment it happens, stamped, retrievable, backed by a document. Using it should feel like closing a filing-cabinet drawer that locks with a satisfying click.

palette.note: Archival blue marks only what is documented and deductible, while unclassified trips and receipts wait in gray until a swipe files them, so the screen itself shows how audit-ready you are.

personal-finance-8.typography: Atlas Grotesk sets the interface and Atlas Typewriter sets every amount, date and merchant line, giving each entry the fixed-width certainty of a record that has been officially filed.
personal-finance-8.motif: The perforated tear-line: every captured receipt and classified trip carries a punched perforation along its edge, the physical mark of a document that now exists in the vault and can be produced on demand.

ia.coreObject: the documented deduction, a trip or receipt with its proof attached
ia.primaryLoop: Drives log themselves in the background; the person swipes them business or personal at a red light and snaps receipts at the counter, and every swipe visibly grows the quarter's deduction total.

recipes-meal-planning-2.territory: The person is on the couch or standing at the counter with a 40-second TikTok they will absolutely lose by Friday, half-inspired and half-annoyed that the recipe exists only as narration. The interface answers with bright kitchen daylight and the satisfaction of a fair transcription: it did the listening, it shows its work frame by frame, and the video is suddenly a real document.

palette.note: Cool daylight neutrals let the video stills carry all the food color; tomato red is spent only on record-style moments — importing, confirming, saving.

recipes-meal-planning-2.typography: GT America for quantities and interface, Value Serif for recipe titles; titles read like a cookbook while everything around them reads like a fast kitchen tool.
recipes-meal-planning-2.motif: The frame-grab receipt: every extracted ingredient carries a tiny rounded still from the exact video moment it was heard or read, like a receipt proving where each line came from.

ia.coreObject: The captured recipe: ingredients and steps assembled from a video's narration, on-screen text, and caption, with the original video attached
ia.primaryLoop: Share a video from TikTok or Instagram, approve the extracted recipe in under a minute, cook from the collection on the weekend; the growing shelf of rescued recipes is the pull.

ride-hailing-1.territory: It is 11:40 pm, the driver is parked outside a closed mall deciding whether one more hour is worth it, tired of apps that guess. The interface answers with dashboard certainty: one hard number per hour, miles counted like an odometer counts them, nothing decorative between the driver and the money. Street energy, but the calm kind you feel when the meter is on your side.

palette.note: Asphalt black keeps glare off the windshield at night, and hi-vis road-marking amber is spent only on verified money and verified miles, never on chrome.

ride-hailing-1.typography: Barlow Semi Condensed for labels and headers with IBM Plex Mono tabular figures for every dollar and mile, so numbers line up like an odometer and read at a glance from a phone mount.
ride-hailing-1.motif: The lane dash: a dashed amber line, like highway paint, that runs under every verified figure and literally ticks segment by segment as background miles accrue.

sleep-tracking-3.territory: It is 2 a.m., the partner is snoring again, and the user is awake, resentful, and fumbling for a volume slider in the dark. The interface answers with the stillness of deep night: near-black indigo, moonlight-soft data, and the reassurance that the volume knob is now handled by something that never sleeps. Everything glows just enough to be read with one half-open eye.

palette.note: Deep-indigo night with a moon-silver accent; brightness is the information channel, the masking envelope literally glows brighter as it swells over a snore burst and dims back in silence, and nothing on the night screen exceeds candlelight luminance.

sleep-tracking-3.typography: Manrope in light and regular weights throughout; soft terminals and generous letterspacing keep even the morning numbers feeling like a whisper rather than a report card.
sleep-tracking-3.motif: The breathing envelope: a soft luminous band across the night timeline that swells over each covered snore burst and settles flat in silence, the product's entire behavior drawn as one calm shape.

ia.coreObject: The night (a timeline of bursts covered by the envelope)
ia.primaryLoop: Set the phone on the nightstand, sleep while the mask rises and falls on its own, and check the morning count of covered bursts; the nightly ritual of 'start night' and the morning proof are the whole habit.

screens.title: Set the stage
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: phone placement and output check, the two things that make or break the mechanic.

screens.title: One night to learn the room

screens.hero: The envelope motif drawn flat with a dotted 'learning' overlay
screens.data: 'Tonight we listen and learn: your room's baseline and your partner's typical volume. The mask stays at a fixed gentle level for this one night. From tomorrow it moves on its own.' Button: 'Start calibration night'

screens.title: Before the first night

screens.purpose: The set-once controls: where the mask starts reacting and the loudest it may ever get.
screens.hero: Two vertical sliders framing a live preview of the envelope's range
screens.data: Trigger threshold: 'above your room baseline, currently sensitive to bursts louder than 48 dB'. Volume ceiling: 62% of max, note 'the mask will never exceed this, even at the loudest snore'. Learned from calibration: 'partner's typical burst 57 to 64 dB'

screens.data: Brown noise (selected), Fan, Rain. Tilt slider: 'darker, more rumble' to 'brighter, more hiss', set 30% toward rumble. Preview plays at tonight's floor level. Note: 'This is the sound at rest; bursts raise its volume, not its character'

screens.data: Time 2:47, envelope currently raised: 'covering a burst, 58%'. Tonight so far: 9 bursts covered. Floor level: 12%. One oversized button: 'Pause sound'. Total screen luminance kept below reading-light level

voice-recorder-4.territory: The user is mid-meeting, half-listening, half-dreading the 20 minutes of reformatting that usually follows. The interface answers with recording-studio composure: one glowing meter, zero clutter, and the quiet promise that the document is already assembling itself in the background. Relief is the product; the UI performs calm competence so the user can stay present in the room.

palette.note: Studio-console charcoal stays matte and even; the single record-red accent is reserved for the live capture state, while export success borrows the destination app's own icon color so 'it landed' reads instantly.

voice-recorder-4.typography: IBM Plex Sans for UI and IBM Plex Mono for timestamps and word counts; the mono figures give every timecode the fixed, trustworthy rhythm of studio gear.
voice-recorder-4.motif: The resolving waveform: live audio bars visibly settle into horizontal text lines and bullet points as the draft assembles, so sound literally becomes document on screen.
